documents.deep: 01 基本信息 标题 ：A role for CIZ1, a Nuclear Matrix Protein Overexpressed in Cancer Cells, in Controlling the Initiation of DNA Replication 作者 ：Hossain, Manzar; Tramantano, Michael; Naik, Sanjay; Stillman, Bruce 单位 ：未提供（根据作者姓名及期刊类型推测为冷泉港实验室（Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory）相关团队，但原文未明确标注，故标注为未提供） 期刊/平台 ：bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 年份 ：2026（预印本发布日期为2026-11-08） 论文类型 ：预印本（preprint） 领域 ：DNA复制起始调控、细胞周期、核基质蛋白、癌症生物学 关键词 ：CIZ1、DNA replication licensing、ORC、CDC6、Cyclin-CDK、CTCF、染色质结构、结直肠癌 DOI/ID ：10.64898/2026.10.10.758243 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（CRISPR tiling screen 数据、RNA-seq 数据等未说明是否公开） 阅读日期 ：2026-11-09（按当前日期推算） 在「cpdch基因家族」方向中的位置 ：本文研究对象为 CIZ1（CDKN1A interacting zinc finger protein 1），与 cpdch 基因家族无直接同源关系，但 CIZ1 作为核基质蛋白参与 DNA 复制许可与染色质结构调控，其与 ORC/CDC6/Cyclin-CDK 的互作机制、CRISPR tiling 筛选策略及急性降解系统（如 auxin-inducible degron）可为 cpdch 基因家族的功能研究提供方法学与机制类比参考。 02 一句话总结 本文通过生化互作、细胞周期分析、CRISPR tiling 筛选及急性降解实验，证明 CIZ1 通过其 C 端锌指区域与 ORC1/CDC6 及 Cyclin E/A-CDK2 直接互作，协调 DNA 复制许可与 S 期进程，并意外发现 CIZ1 维持特定基因组位点的 CTCF 占据，从而将 DNA 复制与染色质高级结构连接，且 CIZ1 缺失显著抑制结直肠癌异种移植瘤生长。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：CIZ1 作为核基质蛋白，在 DNA 复制起始（licensing）中是否发挥直接调控作用？其分子机制是什么？在癌细胞中过表达的 CIZ1 是否成为增殖依赖因子？ 为什么重要 ：DNA 复制许可必须与细胞周期严格偶联以保证基因组稳定性；CIZ1 在多种癌症中过表达，但此前其功能主要与细胞周期蛋白 A 相互作用及核基质结构相关，缺乏其在复制起始中直接作用的证据。理解 CIZ1 的机制可为癌症治疗提供新靶点。 现有方法为何不足 ：此前研究多聚焦于 ORC、CDC6、MCM 等经典 licensing 因子，对核基质蛋白如何参与复制起始的时空协调知之甚少；CIZ1 的已知互作（如与 Cyclin A）未与复制起始机制直接关联。 精确研究问题 ：Can CIZ1 directly coordinate DNA replication licensing through interactions with ORC1, CDC6, and Cyclin-CDK2, and does its overexpression in cancer cells create a dependency that can be therapeutically exploited? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一：DNA 复制许可的经典模型 （1990s–2000s）：ORC 结合复制起点，招募 CDC6 与 CDT1，装载 MCM2-7 解旋酶，形成 pre-RC。代表性方法：酵母遗传学、非洲爪蟾卵提取物。优点：建立了核心框架；局限：对哺乳动物细胞中核基质/染色质环境如何影响 licensing 理解不足。 阶段二：Cyclin-CDK 对 licensing 的调控 （2000s–2010s）：CDK 磷酸化 ORC、CDC6 等抑制 re-licensing，确保每周期仅复制一次。代表性方法：体外激酶实验、磷酸化位点突变。优点：阐明细胞周期偶联；局限：对支架蛋白如何整合 CDK 信号与复制机器缺乏认识。 阶段三：核基质与复制工厂 （2010s–2020s）：核基质蛋白（如 lamin、SATB1）被认为组织复制位点，但直接分子机制不清。CIZ1 曾被报道与 Cyclin A 互作，但功能未明。 本文主张的位置 ：将 CIZ1 确立为核基质上的「分子支架」，直接桥接 ORC1/CDC6 与 Cyclin-CDK2，并意外连接 CTCF 介导的染色质结构，从而整合 licensing、细胞周期信号与基因组组织。 脉络核验状态 ：以上脉络为「仅本文框架」——基于本文引言与讨论的归纳，未逐一核验外部文献。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 Licensing 与细胞周期偶联的分子机制不完整 已知 ORC/CDC6/CDK 互作，但缺乏支架蛋白整合信号 核基质蛋白可能提供空间平台，但此前未鉴定具体因子 摘要：CIZ1 直接与 ORC、CDC6、Cyclin-CDK2 互作 CIZ1 功能不清 过表达于癌症，但机制未知 缺乏系统性功能研究 摘要：CRISPR tiling 筛选鉴定 C 端区域为增殖必需 复制与染色质结构如何连接 复制起始与 CTCF 边界功能看似独立 CIZ1 可能作为双重功能支架 摘要：急性降解导致 CTCF 占据改变及转录程序变化 癌症治疗靶点需求 需识别癌细胞特异性依赖 CIZ1 过表达可能形成非致癌基因依赖 摘要：CIZ1 缺失抑制结直肠癌异种移植瘤生长 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：通过免疫共沉淀（co-IP）鉴定 CIZ1 与 ORC1/CDC6/Cyclin-CDK2 的互作；利用细胞周期同步化分析互作动态；通过 siRNA/shRNA 或急性降解系统（如 auxin-inducible degron）耗尽 CIZ1，检测 MCM 装载、DNA 合成、S 期进程；使用 CRISPR tiling 扫描 C 端功能域；在异种移植模型中验证肿瘤生长依赖。 核心洞察 ：CIZ1 的 C 端锌指区域同时结合 ORC1/CDC6 的 cyclin-binding motif（Cy motif）和 Cyclin-CDK2，形成「CDK 信号-复制起始机器」的物理桥梁；其磷酸化状态动态调控互作，从而将 licensing 与细胞周期状态耦合。此外，CIZ1 的急性降解揭示其独立于复制功能的 CTCF 维持作用，提示该蛋白是「复制-染色质结构」的双功能节点。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：核基质/支架蛋白可能通过「多价互作」同时整合酶促信号与结构组织，此类蛋白的急性降解（而非长期敲除）可揭示其瞬时功能，避免代偿效应；CRISPR tiling 可精确定位功能必需区域，为靶向治疗提供结构基础。 07 方法总览 输入 ：人源细胞系（推测为 U2OS、HCT116 等，原文未明确列出）、结直肠癌细胞系、异种移植小鼠模型。 输出 ：CIZ1 与复制因子的互作图谱、CIZ1 功能必需区域、CTCF 占据变化、肿瘤生长抑制数据。 模块 ： 1. 互作鉴定（co-IP + 免疫印迹） 2. 细胞周期同步化（如双胸苷阻断） 3. 功能缺失（siRNA/shRNA 或急性降解） 4. 复制功能检测（MCM 装载、EdU 掺入、流式细胞术） 5. CRISPR tiling 筛选 6. 转录组分析（RNA-seq） 7. 异种移植实验 训练 ：不适用（非机器学习方法）。 工具 ：未提供具体试剂或仪器清单。 反馈回路 ：CRISPR tiling 筛选结果指导功能域验证；急性降解表型指导 CTCF 机制研究。 文字流程 ：首先通过 co-IP 确认 CIZ1 与 ORC1/CDC6/Cyclin-CDK2 互作 → 定位互作区域（C 端锌指）→ 验证磷酸化调控 → 耗尽 CIZ1 检测复制表型 → CRISPR tiling 确认功能必需区域 → 急性降解检测 CTCF 占据与转录 → 异种移植验证肿瘤依赖。 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 CIZ1-ORC1/CDC6 互作鉴定 确认物理结合 建立 CIZ1 与复制起始机器的直接联系 输入：细胞裂解液；输出：互作条带 C 端区域与 ORC1/CDC6 及 Cyclin-CDK2 互作，其缺失损害复制许可并改变 CTCF 占据，且在结直肠癌异种移植模型中抑制肿瘤生长；但直接互作与体内机制仍需进一步验证。 12 作者自认局限 在提供的材料（摘要）中未发现作者明确承认的局限。 - 作者提及的相关约束 （非正式局限）：摘要中未讨论实验限制，但可推断：未提供细胞系名称、样本量、统计细节；未进行纯化蛋白互作验证；未区分 基因家族成员若定位于核基质或染色质，可能类似地整合细胞周期信号与 DNA 代谢机器。可检查 cpdch 蛋白是否含有 cyclin-binding motif（如 RxL）或 CDK 磷酸化位点。 方法迁移 ：CRISPR tiling 扫描策略可直接用于 cpdch 基因家族，以无偏方式鉴定功能必需结构域，尤其适用于功能未知的家族成员。 方法迁移 ：急性降解系统（如 auxin-inducible degron）适用于 cpdch 基因，可避免长期敲除的代偿效应，揭示其在细胞周期或应激中的瞬时功能。 概念迁移 ：CTCF 占据维持功能提示 cpdch 基因可能也参与染色质结构调控；可测试 cpdch 蛋白是否与 CTCF 或 cohesin 共定位。 实验设计迁移 ：异种移植模型验证癌症相关性，若 cpdch 基因在特定癌症中过表达，可类似评估其作为治疗靶点的潜力。 机制类比 ：CIZ1 的磷酸化调控互作动态，提示 cpdch 蛋白的翻译后修饰（如磷酸化）可能调控其与复制或修复因子的结合，值得进行磷酸化位点扫描。 15 与已有知识连接 相似领域 ：CIZ1 与 ORC/CDC6 的互作类似于已知的 pre-RC 组装因子（如 CDT1 与 CDC6 的互作），可参考经典 licensing 文献（如 Bell & Dutta, 2002, Annu Rev Biochem）。 组合领域 ：CIZ1 的核基质定位与 CTCF 功能连接，可联系核基质/染色质架构蛋白（如 SATB1、lamin B）在基因调控中的角色（如 Cai et al., 2006, Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol）。 冲突领域 ：若 cpdch ：2026年11月（根据预印本日期推断） 在「cpdch基因家族」方向中的位置 ：本文直接研究Chd4（即cpdch基因家族核心成员）及其在ChAHP复合物中的功能，是cpdch基因家族在视网膜发育中功能解析的关键文献。该文通过条件性敲除策略，区分了Chd4依赖ChAHP复合物与非ChAHP依赖（即NuRD复合物）的功能，为理解cpdch基因家族成员在不同组织中的功能分工提供了重要范式。 02 一句话总结 本文通过视网膜特异性条件性敲除Adnp和Chd4，结合组织学、scRNA-seq和CUT&RUN-seq，发现Adnp主要通过ChAHP复合物调控视网膜生长（祖细胞增殖与存活），而Chd4还通过NuRD复合物独立调控细胞命运决定，表明视网膜发育中Chd4的功能大部分不依赖ChAHP。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：ChAHP染色质重塑复合物的两个亚基Adnp和Chd4在视网膜发育中分别发挥什么功能？它们的功能是共同的（通过ChAHP复合物）还是分化的（各自独立）？ 为什么重要 ：ADNP和CHD4均与神经发育障碍（HVDAS和SIHIWES综合征）密切相关，且两者共享相似的表观遗传特征。理解它们在神经发育中的共同与分化功能，对阐明这些疾病的发病机制至关重要。此外，视网膜是研究神经祖细胞命运决定的理想模型系统。 现有方法不足 ：Adnp和Chd4的种系敲除均导致早期胚胎致死（Adnp约E9，Chd4在植入前），无法研究其在神经发育后期的功能。脑-wide条件性敲除（Nestin-Cre）也因围产期致死而无法进行后期分析。此前在端脑（Emx1-Cre）的研究显示Adnp和Chd4表型高度相似，但其他脑区是否如此尚不清楚。 精确研究问题 ：Can conditional ablation of Adnp versus Chd4 in the developing retina reveal common (ChAHP-dependent) versus divergent (ChAHP-independent) functions in retinal growth and cell fate specification? 04 背景与发展脉络 ：本研究仅涉及视网膜发育（E11至P21），不涵盖其他脑区或成年期功能。 基因范围 ：仅研究了Adnp和Chd4两个基因，未涉及ChAHP复合物中HP1亚基（Cbx1/3/5）的功能。 条件性敲除的时空限制 ：Chx10-Cre从E11开始在视网膜祖细胞中表达，因此无法评估Adnp/Chd4在E11之前的视网膜发育（如视泡形成）中的功能。 Adnp cKO的残留表达 ：Adnp蛋白在cKO中"strongly reduced"而非完全消失，不能排除残留蛋白的部分功能。 Chd4 cKO的复杂性 ：Chd4同时是ChAHP和NuRD复合物的亚基，其敲除表型不能简单归因于任一复合物的功能丧失。 端脑与视网膜的比较 ：本文结果与端脑研究（Clémot-Dupont et al., 2024）的差异提示ChAHP功能具有区域特异性，但直接跨脑区比较需谨慎，因为使用的Cre驱动子不同（Emx1-Cre vs Chx10-Cre）。 临床相关性 ：虽然ADNP和CHD4突变与神经发育障碍相关，但本文的完全敲除模型不能直接模拟人类中的单倍剂量不足或显性负效突变。 有边界的复述 ：在视网膜发育中，Adnp通过ChAHP复合物促进祖细胞增殖和存活以支持视网膜生长，而Chd4还通过NuRD复合物独立调控细胞命运决定；ChAHP复合物在视网膜中的功能主要限于生长调控，而非细胞类型规格决定。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 Adnp cKO中残留蛋白表达 Adnp蛋白"strongly reduced"而非完全敲除 未明确提及 Results ：在同一个发育系统（视网膜）中，用相同的Cre驱动子分别敲除同一复合物的不同亚基，通过表型比较区分复合物整体功能与亚基独立功能。这是解析多亚基复合物功能组织的有效范式，可迁移到cpdch基因家族其他成员（如Chd3、Chd5）的功能研究。 多组学交叉验证 ：将表型分析（组织学）、转录组（scRNA-seq）、基因组结合（CUT&RUN-seq）和蛋白质互作（coIP-MS）四种维度结合，从不同层面验证同一结论。对于cpdch基因家族研究，可借鉴此策略系统比较不同家族成员的功能。 基因注释陷阱 ：Adnp的readthrough转录本（与Dpm1融合）导致表达数据中Adnp信号缺失，这是一个重要的技术警示。在研究cpdch基因家族时，需检查是否存在类似的基因注释问题（如反义转录本、readthrough转录本、假基因干扰）。 补偿效应的考虑 ：Chd4敲除后Chd3/Chd5上调，提示cpdch基因家族成员间可能存在功能补偿。在设计敲除实验时，需同时检测其他家族成员的表达变化。 Ctcf在ChAHP功能中的潜在角色 ：Adnp和Chd4在Ctcf位点共占据，且Chd4敲除后Ctcf占据增加，提示ChAHP可能通过调控Ctcf结合来影响染色质结构。这为cpdch基因家族与绝缘子功能的关系提供了新线索。 区域特异性功能 ：同一复合物在不同脑区（端脑vs视网膜）的功能权重不同，提示研究cpdch基因家族时需考虑组织特异性，不能简单跨组织外推。 scRNA-seq聚类作为表型读出 ：作者通过聚类分析发现cKO细胞进入"新型"聚类，提示转录组状态偏移可作为表型变化的敏感指标，即使传统组织学未显示明显差异。 15 与已有知识连接 ChAHP复合物的原始发现 ：Ostapcuk et al. 该研究针对一个具有重要神经发育疾病相关性的染色质重塑复合物，在视网膜发育模型中进行了系统的功能解剖。研究设计合理，采用了多种互补技术（遗传学、转录组学、基因组学、蛋白质组学），并利用了作者此前建立的皮层模型进行比较。核心发现——Adnp和Chd4在视网膜中功能分化——具有新颖性和潜在的重要临床意义。然而，当前版本存在几个关键问题：scRNA-seq整合分析的批次效应控制方法需要更严格的验证；Adnp cKO中Chd4蛋白水平下降的机制未阐明；cut&run-seq数据的定量比较缺乏统计框架。这些问题的解决对于支撑"Chd4具有ChAHP非依赖性功能"的核心结论至关重要。 Who would be interested in the results, and why 神经发育生物学和表观遗传学领域的研究者会对该研究感兴趣，特别是关注染色质重塑复合物在脑区特异性功能的研究组。此外，由于ADNP和CHD4与自闭症谱系障碍和智力障碍的强遗传关联，研究神经发育疾病机制的转化医学研究者也会关注。视网膜作为中枢神经系统的可及模型，该研究为理解脑区特异性染色质调控机制提供了比较框架。 Major strengths 1) 研究设计具有明确的比较逻辑，通过同一驱动系（Chx10-Cre）在相同发育时间点敲除两个亚基，使表型差异可直接归因于基因功能差异；2) 多组学整合策略（scRNA-seq + cut&run-seq + 已发表ATAC-seq）提供了从基因组定位到转录输出的完整证据链；3) 基因家族。但其核心范式——「代谢酶-染色质修饰-剪接因子-表型」的因果链解析、亚型特异性调控、代谢物驱动的组蛋白修饰开关——为 cpdch 基因家族研究提供了可迁移的方法论框架和机制研究模板。 02 一句话总结 本文通过整合 scRNA-seq、ChIP-seq、ATAC-seq、RNA-seq 及多种生化实验，证明在缺氧乳腺癌中 CTCF 通过驱动糖酵解基因表达和 LDHB 的细胞类型特异性调控，决定核内乳酸可用性，进而通过 H3K18la/H3K18ac 的互斥修饰开关，在 TACC3 外显子 3 下游的 CTCF 结合位点（CBSDS）招募不同的 reader-splicing factor 复合物（SMARCA4-hnRNPA1 或 TRIM33-SRSF10），最终在 TNBC 中促进外显子包含（FL 亚型，干细胞性）而非 TNBC 中促进外显子跳跃（Δ3 亚型，EMT）。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：在缺氧乳腺癌中，代谢状态（乳酸产生）如何通过组蛋白乳酸化修饰差异性地调控可变剪接，且这种调控为何在不同乳腺癌亚型（TNBC vs 非 TNBC）中产生相反的剪接结果？ 为什么重要 ：乳酸在肿瘤中积累并驱动组蛋白乳酸化已被认识，但「为什么糖酵解速率相当的肿瘤乳酸化水平不同」以及「乳酸化如何转化为特定的剪接决策」尚不清楚。TNBC 的侵袭性和化疗耐药与干细胞特性密切相关，理解其代谢-表观-剪接轴的调控机制可能揭示新的治疗靶点。 现有方法不足 ：已有研究主要关注乳酸化的全局水平与基因表达调控，缺乏对「核内乳酸池」这一更近端决定因素的解析；缺乏将代谢酶（LDHB）与染色质架构蛋白（CTCF）联系起来的机制框架；缺乏对乳酸化/乙酰化在同一残基上互斥竞争的剪接层面功能后果的研究。 精确研究问题 ：Can a CTCF-LDHB axis determine nuclear lactate availability and thereby switch H3K18 acylation state (lactylation vs acetylation) at an intragenic CTCF binding site to direct alternative splicing of TACC3 exon 3 in a breast cancer subtype-specific manner? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络为「仅本文框架」，基于本文引文与叙述逻辑整理，未经外部核验。 阶段一：乳酸作为代谢废物 → 信号分子 。Warburg 效应确立了肿瘤糖酵解增强和乳酸分泌的特征。近年研究将乳酸从代谢副产物提升为信号分子，可修饰组蛋白赖氨酸残基（乳酸化，lactylation），将代谢状态与染色质状态直接耦合。 阶段二：组蛋白乳酸化的表观遗传功能 。研究证明乳酸化（如 H3K18la）在巨噬细胞、肿瘤等场景中调控基因表达，且与乙酰化（H3K18ac）在同一残基上竞争。但乳酸化的上游调控（什么决定乳酸化水平）和下游功能（除转录外是否调控其他染色质过程）尚不清楚。 阶段三：CTCF 作为代谢-剪接耦合的候选节点 。作者前期工作（引用 9-12）已证明 CTCF 在缺氧下发生基因组重分布，并通过诱导 Pol II 暂停调控可变剪接。本文在此框架上引入代谢维度，提出 CTCF 不仅直接调控剪接，还通过控制代谢基因表达（糖酵解、LDHB）设定核内乳酸水平，从而决定局部组蛋白修饰状态。 本文主张的位置 ：将 CTCF 从「染色质架构因子」扩展为「代谢-表观-剪接」三者的整合枢纽；将 LDHB 从「代谢酶」扩展为「核内乳酸池的负调控因子」；提出 H3K18la/ac 作为「代谢开关」在剪接层面发挥亚型特异性功能。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 scRNA-seq 数据（GSE165929）分析 CTCF 与糖酵解基因的相关性； - 在 MCF7（非 TNBC）和 MDA-MB-231（TNBC）细胞系中进行缺氧处理，结合 ATAC-seq、CTCF ChIP-seq、H3K18la/H3K18ac ChIP-seq、RNA-seq 等多组学分析； - 通过 shRNA 敲低 CTCF、LDHB、ERα、SMARCA4、TRIM33、SRS10、hnRNPA1 等，结合剪接报告实验、核内乳酸测定、类器官/球体形成实验、体内肿瘤模型，验证因果链。 2) 核心洞察 ： - 核内乳酸池而非总乳酸决定乳酸化水平 ：LDHB 通过消耗核内乳酸，将「糖酵解速率」与「组蛋白乳酸化」解耦，是乳酸化水平的隐藏调控节点。 - CTCF 是代谢-表观-剪接的整合器 ：CTCF 既驱动糖酵解基因表达（产生乳酸），又通过调控 LDHB 决定乳酸消耗，同时其自身结合位点（CBSDS）是 H3K18 修饰的落点，形成「CTCF→LDHB→核内乳酸→H3K18la/ac→剪接因子招募→剪接决策」的完整因果链。 - 同一 CTCF 位点、同一组蛋白残基，通过不同修饰招募不同 reader，产生相反剪接结果 ：H3K18la 招募 SMARCA4-hnRNPA1 促进外显子跳跃（Δ3，EMT）；H3K18ac 招募 TRIM33-SRSF10 促进外显子包含（FL，干细胞性）。这构成了一个「代谢开关决定剪接方向」的机制范式。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ： - 代谢酶的表达水平（而非仅代谢物总量）可能是表观遗传修饰更直接的调控变量；研究组蛋白修饰时应关注「底物在亚细胞区室中的可用性」而非全局代谢物浓度。 - 同一转录因子（CTCF）可通过控制代谢基因表达来间接设定自身结合位点的修饰状态，形成「转录因子→代谢→表观→剪接」的自洽调控回路，这种回路可能广泛存在于其他代谢敏感的发育和疾病场景。 - 亚型/细胞类型特异性的剪接差异，可能源于上游转录因子组合（如 CTCF-ERα）对代谢基因的差异调控，而非剪接因子本身的差异表达。 07 方法总览 输入 ：缺氧（1% O₂）处理的 MCF7（非 TNBC）和 MDA-MB-231（TNBC）乳腺癌细胞系；已发表 scRNA-seq 数据（GSE165929）；患者肿瘤组织样本；小鼠 4T1 同系移植瘤模型。 输出 ：TACC3 外显子 3 剪接开关的分子机制模型；LDHB 作为 TNBC 治疗靶点的体内验证数据。 主要模块 ： 1. 多组学分析 ：scRNA-seq（CTCF-糖酵解相关性）、ATAC-seq（染色质可及性）、CTCF ChIP-seq、H3K18la/H3K18ac ChIP-seq、RNA-seq（基因表达与剪接）； 2. 功能扰动 ：shRNA 敲低 CTCF、LDHB、ERα、SMARCA4、TRIM33、SRS10、hnRNPA1；过表达 LDHB、MCT1； 3. 生化与分子实验 ：核内/胞质乳酸分离测定、ChIP-qPCR、RNA免疫沉淀（RIP）、PAR-CLIP-qRT-PCR、荧光素酶报告基因（LDHB 启动子）、位点定向突变（CTCF/ERα 结合位点）、免疫印迹； 4. 表型实验 ：mammosphere 形成实验（干细胞性）、Transwell 侵袭实验（EMT）、3D 球体侵袭、体内肿瘤生长实验（4T1 同系模型）； 5. 蛋白质互作 ：邻近连接实验（PLA）验证 SMARCA4-hnRNPA1、CTCF-hnRNPA1、TRIM33-SRSF10 互作。 训练/基准 ：不适用（非机器学习方法）。 反馈回路 ：敲低/过表达后的剪接表型与 H3K18 修饰状态互为验证；体外细胞实验与体内肿瘤模型互为验证。 假设 ：H3K18la 与 H3K18ac 在同一残基上互斥；核内乳酸浓度是 H3K18la 的直接决定因素；CTCF 结合位点的局部修饰状态可被 reader 蛋白识别并影响剪接因子招募。 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 CTCF-糖酵解基因调控模块 CTCF 结合糖酵解基因（SLC2A3/GLUT3、PFKFB3）启动子，驱动其缺氧诱导表达 建立 CTCF 与乳酸产生的因果联系 输入：缺氧处理、CTCF ：本文最核心的可迁移概念是——组蛋白修饰的水平不由细胞总代谢物浓度决定，而由特定亚细胞区室（细胞核）中的代谢物可用性决定。LDHB 通过消耗核内乳酸，在总乳酸不变的情况下改变 H3K18la 水平。 迁移到 cpdch 方向 ：若 cpdch 基因家族涉及代谢酶或转运蛋白，应关注其在细胞核/细胞质中的分布差异，而非仅测量全细胞代谢物水平。 转录因子-代谢酶-组蛋白修饰-剪接的完整因果链解析策略 ：本文提供了一个从「转录因子（CTCF）→代谢酶（LDHB）→代谢物（核内乳酸）→组蛋白修饰（H3K18la/ac）→reader 蛋白（SMARCA4/TRIM33）→剪接因子（hnRNPA1/SRSF10）→剪接事件（TACC3 外显子 3）→表型（干细胞性/EMT）」的七层因果链研究模板。 迁移到 cpdch 方向 ：若 cpdch 基因家族参与代谢-表观调控，可沿此链条逐层验证。 同一残基的互斥修饰作为「开关」机制 ：H3K18 的乳酸化与乙酰化在同一残基上竞争，且两种修饰招募不同的 reader 蛋白，产生相反的剪接结果。这种「竞争性修饰-不同 reader-相反功能」的开关模型，可能适用于其他代谢物来源的酰化修饰（如丁酰化、丙酰化等）。 迁移到 cpdch 方向 ：若 cpdch 基因家族涉及酰化修饰酶，可检验其底物特异性是否通过竞争性修饰实现功能切换。 亚型特异性调控源于上游转录因子组合 ：CTCF 单独存在时驱动 LDHB 表达，但与 ERα 形成复合物后反而抑制 LDHB。同一转录因子在不同细胞类型中因辅因子不同而产生相反调控。 迁移到 cpdch 方向 ：研究 cpdch 基因家族在不同亚型/细胞类型中的差异功能时，应关注其与细胞类型特异性转录因子的互作，而非仅关注其自身表达水平。 「reader-splicing factor」偶联作为剪接调控的新机制 ：组蛋白修饰不是直接决定剪接，而是通过招募染色质 reader 蛋白，后者再招募剪接因子到 Pol II 暂停位点。这种「修饰-reader-剪接因子」的三级偶联机制，为理解表观遗传如何调控 RNA 加工提供了新框架。 迁移到 cpdch 方向 ：若 cpdch 基因家族编码 reader 蛋白或剪接因子，可检验其是否通过识别特定组蛋白修饰来调控剪接。 体内药理学验证的简洁设计 ：使用单一 LDHB 抑制剂（AXDH-0046）在 4T1 同系模型中同时检测肿瘤生长和干细胞标志物，以最少的动物实验验证了从代谢酶到表型的因果链。 迁移到 cpdch 方向 ：若 cpdch 基因家族有可用抑制剂，可考虑类似的体内验证设计。 15 与已有知识连接 乳酸化修饰的发现 ：Zhang et al. (2019) 首次报道组蛋白赖氨酸乳酸化（Kla）作为新修饰，由 p300/CBP 催化。本文在此基础上聚焦 H3K18 位点，并引入 LDHB 作为负调控因子，扩展了乳酸化的调控维度。 CTCF 与剪接调控 ：Shukla et al. (2011) 及作者前期工作（引用 9-12）已证明 CTCF 通过诱导 Pol II 暂停调控可变剪接。本文将 CTCF 的剪接调控功能与代谢基因表达调控连接，形成「CTCF→代谢→表观→剪接」的整合模型。 代谢-表观遗传交叉 ：已有研究（如乙酰辅酶A 与组蛋白乙酰化）确立了代谢物作为表观遗传底物的概念。本文的贡献在于提出「核内代谢物池」的区室化调控，而非仅关注全局代谢物浓度。 ERα 与代谢调控 ：ERα 在乳腺癌中的代谢调控功能已有大量研究，但 ERα 与 CTCF 协同调控 LDHB 的机制是新的连接。 TACC3 与肿瘤 ：TACC3 已知参与中心体调控和基因组稳定性，其剪接亚型与肿瘤干细胞/EMT 的关联是本文的新发现。 可迁移领域 ：本文的「代谢酶-组蛋白修饰-剪接」框架可迁移至其他代谢物驱动的酰化修饰（如丁酰化、丙二酰化）研究；「转录因子-代谢酶」的细胞类型特异性调控模式可迁移至其他核受体研究。 16 研究想法 标题：Agent 生成的研究候选 候选 1：cpdch 基因家族成员的亚细胞定位与核内代谢物调控 - Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose that nuclear (not total intracellular) lactate availability sets H3K18 lactylation in breast cancer; that a CTCF–LDHB axis, together with ERα status, determines whether LDHB is expressed (TNBC) or repressed (non-TNBC); that LDHB consumes lactate to favor H3K18 acetylation while CTCF-dependent MCT1 delivers lactate to the nucleus to sustain H3K18la where LDHB is low; and that at a CTCF site downstream of TACC3 exon 3, H3K18la versus H3K18ac recruits distinct reader/splicing-factor complexes (SMARCA4–hnRNPA1 vs TRIM33–SRSF10) to drive exon skipping (EMT) versus inclusion (stemness), with LDHB inhibition suppressing tumor growth in vivo. Visible evidence base Narrative descriptions of: scRNA-seq reanalysis (GSE165929, GSE161529), ATAC-seq and CTCF ChIP-seq in MCF7, RNA-seq after CTCF depletion, Seahorse ECAR/OCR, dCas9-DNMT3A/HDAC3/AARS1 epigenome editing, luciferase reporter and site-directed mutagenesis, ChIP-qPCR/MeDIP-qPCR, histone mark immunoblotting, nuclear/intracellular/extracellular lactate and pyruvate assays, LDHB overexpression and AXKO-0046 inhibition, PAR-CLIP, proximity ligation assay, confocal imaging, TACC3 isoform functional assays, and a 4T1 syngeneic mouse tumor experiment. All quantitative support resides in figures/tables not provided. Missing materials affecting confidence All main figures (1–15) and supplementary figures (S1–S5); Tables S1–S8; figure legends; raw sequencing data (stated as deposited but "available upon publication"); patient clinicopathological detail (Table S6); antibody and primer tables; any statistical reporting (n, tests, correction) beyond brief mentions. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript describes a mechanistically ambitious, multi-layered model linking CTCF, subtype-specific lactate handling, intragenic histone H3K18 acylation, and co-transcriptional alternative splicing of TACC3, with an in vivo LDHB-inhibition arm. The conceptual framing (nuclear lactate as the proximal determinant; kinetic-plus-adaptor coupling) is coherent and potentially interesting. However, from the supplied text alone, the central causal chain is not established. Several key steps rest on correlative or single-system observations, some internal statements are inconsistent, and critical controls and quantitative detail are not visible. The work is not assessable at the level required to support its headline claims without the figures, tables, and statistics. Who would be interested in the results, and why Cancer metabolism and epigenetics researchers (lactate, lactylation, LDHB, MCT1/MCT4), chromatin and transcription biologists (CTCF, Pol II pausing, histone acylation readers), RNA-processing/splicing groups (co-transcriptional splicing, hnRNPA1, SRSF10, TRIM33, SMARCA4), and breast-cancer translational researchers interested in TNBC subtype-specific vulnerabilities and LDHB as a target. Major strengths A clear, testable central hypothesis that distinguishes nuclear from total lactate as the determinant of H3K18la, which is a meaningful refinement over bulk-lactate framing. Use of orthogonal perturbations (genetic depletion, dCas9-DNMT3A/HDAC3/AARS1 targeted editing, pharmacological LDHB inhibition, overexpression) across two subtype-representative lines. A locus-resolved mechanistic proposal at TACC3 exon 3 that attempts to unify kinetic (Pol II pause) and adaptor (reader plus splicing factor) models. Inclusion of an in vivo tumor-growth arm and patient-sample correlation, which, if supported, would extend the findings beyond cell lines. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Causal inference / central claim Claim pointer Nuclear lactate availability, rather than total intracellular lactate, determines H3K18 lactylation, and LDHB sets this balance. Evidence pointer Results sections on LDHB and H3K18la (Figure 5, Figure 6); location not provided for underlying data. Concern The nuclear-versus-total distinction is supported by comparing two cell lines that differ in many respects beyond LDHB (ER status, glycolytic rate, transporter repertoire). The causal test relies on LDHB overexpression in MCF7 and AXKO-0046 in MDA-MB-231, but the text does not report whether nuclear lactate and H3K18la changes were dissociated from total lactate changes, nor whether the inhibitor's effects are on-target and LDHB-specific. The claim that nuclear lactate is "the more proximal determinant" is asserted rather than demonstrated by an experiment that holds total lactate constant while varying nuclear lactate. Why it matters The central novelty of the paper depends on nuclear lactate being the operative pool. If the observations are equally explained by total lactate, subtype background, or off-target inhibitor effects, the framing collapses to a less distinctive claim. Resolution test Show that manipulating nuclear lactate import/export (e.g., MCT1/MCT4 or nuclear-targeted perturbations) changes H3K18la while total intracellular lactate is unchanged, and that LDHB rescue/inhibition effects on H3K18la track nuclear rather than total lactate across multiple lines. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic sufficiency / causality at the TACC3 locus Claim pointer At CBSDS downstream of TACC3 exon 3, H3K18la recruits SMARCA4–hnRNPA1 to drive exon skipping, whereas H3K18ac recruits TRIM33–SRSF10 to drive inclusion. Evidence pointer Results sections on TACC3 splicing and reader complexes (Figures 9–12); location not provided. Concern The reader/splicing-factor assignments rest largely on depletion-plus-occupancy and PLA interaction data. The text does not establish direct binding of SMARCA4 to H3K18la or TRIM33 to H3K18ac at this locus, nor that reader recruitment is the causal determinant of the splicing outcome rather than a correlate of the mark. The claim that hnRNPA1 binds a "consensus splicing silencer motif near exon 3" and that SRSF10 "stabilizes 3'/5' splice site recognition" is stated without supporting data in the text. Why it matters The adaptor model is the mechanistic core of the paper. Without direct binding and epistasis evidence, the reader-to-splicing-factor linkage remains a proposed model rather than an established mechanism. Resolution test Provide direct binding assays (e.g., recombinant reader domain with modified vs unmodified H3K18 peptides), reader-domain mutants that abolish mark recognition, and epistasis showing that reader/splicing-factor depletion occludes the mark-dependent splicing switch. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Internal consistency / data integrity Claim pointer CTCF drives LDHB in TNBC and a CTCF–ERα complex represses LDHB in non-TNBC; CTCF is a positive driver of LDHB in both contexts. Evidence pointer Results section on CTCF/ERα/LDHB (Figures 3–4); location not provided. Concern The text contains statements that are difficult to reconcile. It states that CTCF depletion or ESR1-promoter methylation "supported LDHB expression" in MCF7 while also concluding CTCF is a positive driver of LDHB and that ERα converts this into repression. The direction of effect of CTCF loss on LDHB in MCF7 is described inconsistently across the section. Additionally, the model requires CTCF occupancy at the LDHB promoter in both lines yet opposite transcriptional outcomes, which is asserted but not mechanistically resolved beyond the ERα/EZH2/H3K27me2 correlation. Why it matters The subtype-specific LDHB regulation is a load-bearing element of the axis. Contradictory directional statements undermine confidence in the interpretation and in the figure-to-text correspondence. Resolution test Clarify and reconcile the direction of LDHB change upon CTCF loss in MCF7 versus MDA-MB-231 with matched quantification, and demonstrate the repressive complex (ERα–EZH2–H3K27me2) is necessary and sufficient for LDHB repression at the same CTCF-occupied promoter. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis In vivo claim support Claim pointer Inhibiting LDHB restores exon skipping and suppresses tumor growth in vivo, identifying LDHB as a tractable target in TNBC. Evidence pointer Results section on in vivo LDHB inhibition (Figure 14); Methods "Animal Experiments"; location not provided. Concern The in vivo experiment uses 4T1 (murine TNBC) cells and AXKO-0046, but the text does not report whether tumor reduction is accompanied by the proposed molecular mechanism in vivo (TACC3 isoform switching, H3K18la/ac status, target engagement). The link between tumor growth suppression and the CTCF–LDHB–TACC3 axis is asserted rather than demonstrated. Group sizes, randomization detail, and statistical power are not provided in the text. Why it matters The therapeutic conclusion depends on the in vivo effect being mechanistically attributable to the proposed axis, not to general LDHB inhibition or off-target toxicity. Resolution test Show target engagement and pathway readouts (TACC3 splicing, H3K18la/ac, stemness markers) in treated tumors, with adequate n, randomization, and blinded quantification, and demonstrate that the axis mediates the growth effect. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Specificity of pharmacological and epigenetic tools Claim pointer AXKO-0046 specifically inhibits LDHB; dCas9-HDAC3 removes H3K18la; dCas9-AARS1 writes H3K18la. Evidence pointer Results sections on LDHB inhibition and targeted editing (Figures 6, 10); Methods "dcas9-mediated epigenome editing"; location not provided. Concern The text does not report selectivity controls for AXKO-0046 (e.g., LDHB vs LDHA), nor global versus locus-specific effects of dCas9-HDAC3 and dCas9-AARS1. HDAC3 has broad deacetylase activity and AARS1 has reported roles beyond H3K18la; the claim of mark-specific, locus-restricted action is not substantiated in the supplied text. Why it matters If the tools are not mark- or target-specific, the causal inferences about H3K18la/ac at CBSDS are weakened. Resolution test Provide selectivity data (dose-response, LDHA/LDHB isoform-specific readouts, catalytically dead dCas9-fusion controls, global histone mark immunoblotting) demonstrating locus-restricted and mark-specific effects. Concern ID R1-M6 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility / statistical reporting Claim pointer Genome-wide and locus-specific conclusions across RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, and functional assays. Evidence pointer Throughout Results; Methods "RNA-seq data analysis", "ChIP-seq data analyses"; location not provided. Concern The text reports few replicate numbers, effect sizes, or statistical tests for the sequencing and functional comparisons. Several key claims (e.g., "595 downregulated genes had reduced promoter H3K18ac", differential CTCF occupancy, isoform usage) are stated without visible thresholds, replicate structure, or multiple-testing context in the prose. Data availability states sequencing data will be released only upon publication, limiting independent verification. Why it matters Without replicate and statistical transparency, the robustness of the genome-wide and splicing claims cannot be judged. Resolution test Report n, statistical tests, effect sizes, and thresholds for each key comparison, and make sequencing data available for review. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Nomenclature / clarity Affected element Figure callout "Figure J" in the MCT1 section. Evidence pointer Results section on CTCF/MCT1 (Figure 7); location not provided. Issue The text refers to "Figure J" without a number, which is ambiguous. Required correction Correct the figure callout to the intended panel. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Consistency of cell-line/dataset description Affected element scRNA-seq dataset identifiers. Evidence pointer Results (GSE165929) versus Methods (GSE161529); location not provided. Issue The Results cite GSE165929 while the Methods describe GSE161529, which may be a discrepancy or two different datasets used without clear linkage. Required correction Clarify which dataset underlies each analysis and reconcile the identifiers. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Terminology precision Affected element Use of "acylation" in the title versus "acetylation/lactylation" in the text. Evidence pointer Title; throughout. Issue "Acylation switch" is used broadly; the manuscript specifically addresses H3K18la and H3K18ac. The broader term may overstate generality. Required correction Define acylation scope explicitly or use the specific marks consistently. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Reporting completeness Affected element Patient sample analysis. Evidence pointer Methods "Breast Cancer Patient Samples"; Figure 5D–F; Table S6; location not provided. Issue Sample number, subtype composition, and staging are deferred to a supplementary table not provided; the correlation claim cannot be evaluated. Required correction Report n per subtype and the statistical basis for the LDHB–H3K18la correlation in the main text. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Figure-to-text traceability Affected element Numerous multi-panel figure references. Evidence pointer Throughout Results; location not provided. Issue Many claims are attributed to figure panels that are not supplied, preventing verification of whether the text matches the data. Required correction Ensure each claim maps to a specific, legible panel with quantified replicates. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3, R1-M4 (blocking); R1-M5, R1-M6 (supporting). The nuclear-lactate causal claim, the reader/splicing-factor mechanism, the internal consistency of the LDHB regulation model, and the in vivo mechanistic linkage are the primary unresolved items. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The nuclear-lactate framing and the kinetic-plus-adaptor coupling at a single splicing locus are conceptually distinctive. However, individual components (CTCF and Pol II pausing, histone lactylation, reader-recruited splicing factors) build on prior work, and the incremental novelty depends on the nuclear-versus-total distinction being causally demonstrated, which is not yet established from the text. Scientific importance Potentially significant for TNBC biology and for lactate–chromatin coupling if the mechanism holds. The therapeutic implication (LDHB inhibition) is attractive but currently supported only by an in vivo growth effect without demonstrated mechanistic linkage. Interdisciplinary readership The topic spans metabolism, epigenetics, and RNA processing, which suits a broad audience. The current presentation, with dense locus-level detail and unresolved inconsistencies, would need tightening for non-specialist accessibility. Technical soundness Not established from the supplied material. Key causal steps rely on correlative or single-system evidence, tool specificity is not demonstrated, and statistical/replicate reporting is sparse. Readability for nonspecialists The narrative is generally well organized, but the density of gene/mark/reader nomenclature and the internal inconsistencies reduce clarity for a general readership. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript is potentially supportive if the blocking technical concerns (nuclear-lactate causality, reader/splicing-factor mechanism, internal consistency, in vivo mechanistic linkage) are resolved with direct evidence and full data/statistics. Risk / unsupported claims Unsupported as written Nuclear lactate, rather than total intracellular lactate, is the proximal determinant of H3K18la (no experiment holding total lactate constant while varying nuclear lactate is described). Unsupported as written SMARCA4 is a specific reader of H3K18la and TRIM33 a direct binder of H3K18ac at CBSDS (no direct binding data described; reader identity rests on depletion/occupancy and PLA). Unsupported as written hnRNPA1 binds a consensus silencer motif near exon 3 and SRSF10 stabilizes 3'/5' splice site recognition (asserted without supporting data in the text). Unsupported as written LDHB inhibition suppresses tumor growth through the CTCF–LDHB–TACC3 axis in vivo (no in-tumor pathway readouts or target engagement reported). Weakly supported CTCF is a positive driver of LDHB in both subtypes while ERα converts this to repression (directional statements are internally inconsistent in the text). Weakly supported AXKO-0046 acts specifically on LDHB (no selectivity data described). Weakly supported dCas9-HDAC3 and dCas9-AARS1 act mark-specifically and locus-restrictedly (no catalytically dead or global-mark controls described). Not assessable All genome-wide claims (differential CTCF occupancy, H3K18la/ac enrichment, 595-gene intersection, isoform usage) and all patient-sample correlations, because figures, tables, and statistics were not provided. Not assessable Reproducibility of any result, given absent replicate/statistical reporting and sequencing data withheld until publication.

boundary Evaluation is restricted to the supplied abstract. No methods, figures, tables, supplementary material, or line-level content were available, so mechanistic, statistical, and reproducibility claims cannot be independently verified. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that cfChIP-seq in prostate cancer plasma defines 35,120 modification-associated positions (MAPs) where nucleosomes carrying H3K4me2 (active) and H3K9me3 (repressive) marks occupy reproducibly offset positions; that these offsets recur across marks, an independent cohort, and nuclease-digested cell-line chromatin; that MAPs are enriched in transcribed genes and depleted near TSS and CTCF sites; that nucleosome protection at MAPs correlates with tumor fraction (TF) across 2,535 cfDNA datasets; that a 50-MAP targeted panel distinguishes TF ≥3% from 0% (AUC 0.91-0.96) and outperforms a fragmentomics-based TF predictor; and that MAP protection at ASCL1 sites detects neuroendocrine transformation. Visible evidence base Abstract-level statements only. No primary data, no figure or table references, no statistical detail, no cohort descriptions beyond cancer type mentions. Missing materials affecting confidence Full text, Methods, figures, tables, supplementary data, cohort characteristics, cfChIP-seq quality metrics, antibody validation, statistical models, cross-validation scheme, and independent validation details. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract describes a conceptually interesting extension of cfDNA fragmentomics, namely that histone-modification state may impose reproducible nucleosome positional offsets detectable in plasma. The reported effect sizes (AUC 0.91-0.96, r = 0.89-0.91) and the breadth of the dataset (2,535 cfDNA datasets) are notable if substantiated. However, from the supplied material alone the central claims are not independently assessable. Key concerns include whether the observed offsets are attributable to histone modification per se rather than to underlying sequence, GC content, or chromatin accessibility; whether the cfChIP-seq signal is specific given the low input and antibody-dependent nature of the assay; and whether the reported performance is established on held-out data. The work is potentially of interest but currently rests on unverifiable abstract-level assertions. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in liquid biopsy and cfDNA fragmentomics, epigenetics and chromatin biology, prostate and genitourinary oncology, and computational genomics. If validated, a mutation-independent, histone-modification-informed readout of tumor fraction and cancer state would be relevant to minimal residual disease monitoring, treatment response tracking, and lineage plasticity such as neuroendocrine transformation. Major strengths Addresses a clear biological question, whether cfDNA nucleosome positioning encodes chromatin state and histone modification identity. Reports replication across histone marks, an independent cfChIP-seq cohort, and nuclease-digested cell-line chromatin, which if properly executed strengthens generalizability. Uses a large external corpus (2,535 cfDNA sequencing datasets) for the TF correlation analysis. Demonstrates a potential translational application with a compact 50-MAP panel and comparison against an existing fragmentomics-based predictor. Includes a disease-state application (ASCL1-linked neuroendocrine transformation) that, if robust, would be clinically meaningful. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Causal attribution / confounding Claim pointer Nucleosomes bearing H3K4me2 and H3K9me3 occupy reproducibly offset positions, and these offsets define distinct nucleosome positions attributable to histone modification state. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The abstract does not establish that the positional offsets are caused by or specific to histone modification status rather than to underlying DNA sequence, GC content, nucleosome occupancy, or chromatin accessibility differences that co-vary with these marks. H3K4me2 and H3K9me3 occupy largely distinct genomic compartments, so offset differences could reflect compartment-level sequence or accessibility properties rather than a direct modification-position relationship. Why it matters The central mechanistic claim of the paper depends on this attribution. If offsets are confounded by sequence or accessibility, the interpretation that histone modifications "define" nucleosome positions is not supported. Resolution test Show that offsets persist after controlling for sequence composition, GC content, and accessibility, for example by sequence-matched or accessibility-matched comparisons, or by demonstrating mark-specific offset signatures at the same loci. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Assay specificity / technical validity Claim pointer cfChIP-seq identifies 35,120 modification-associated positions in plasma. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern cfChIP-seq from plasma operates on very low input and depends on antibody specificity and immunoprecipitation efficiency. The abstract provides no information on antibody validation, input amounts, background or input controls, or how nonspecific pull-down was excluded. Without this, the 35,120 MAPs cannot be accepted as modification-associated. Why it matters If the immunoprecipitation is not specific, the MAP set and all downstream analyses, including TF correlation and panel performance, are compromised at the foundation. Resolution test Report antibody validation (for example peptide competition, knockout or spike-in controls), input and IgG controls, replicate concordance, and fraction-of-reads-in-peaks metrics, with a demonstration that MAPs are recovered above background. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical validity / overfitting Claim pointer A 50-MAP model distinguished samples with tumor fractions ≥3% vs 0% with AUCs of 0.91-0.96 across prostate, breast, and lung cancers and outperformed a state-of-the-art fragmentomics-based tumor fraction predictor. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The abstract does not state whether the 50-MAP panel and model were derived and evaluated on independent data, how samples were split, whether cross-validation was used, or how the comparator predictor was trained and tuned. With only 50 features selected from 35,120 candidates, selection bias and overfitting are substantial risks, and the cross-cancer generalization claim requires independent cohorts per cancer type. Why it matters The reported AUCs and the superiority claim over an existing method are only meaningful under a properly held-out evaluation. Without this, the performance figures are not established. Resolution test Provide a pre-specified train/test split or nested cross-validation, report confidence intervals and sample sizes per cancer type, and demonstrate that the comparator was evaluated under equivalent conditions. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Correlation interpretation / confounding by tumor fraction Claim pointer Nucleosome protection at a subset of MAPs correlated with tumor fraction across 2,535 cfDNA datasets, reflecting differences in histone modification status between cancer-derived and non-malignant chromatin. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern Correlation between MAP protection and TF may be driven by global cfDNA fragmentation differences, tumor-derived fragment length distributions, or copy-number effects rather than by histone modification status. The abstract does not describe how TF was estimated, whether the correlation survives adjustment for fragment length and GC, or whether the relationship is monotonic across the TF range. Why it matters The claim that MAP protection reflects modification-status differences between malignant and non-malignant chromatin requires exclusion of generic fragmentomic confounders. Resolution test Report partial correlations or regression adjusting for fragment length, GC content, and copy number, and show that MAP protection adds information beyond these covariates. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Clinical claim support Claim pointer MAP protection at ASCL1 binding sites identified neuroendocrine transformation of prostate cancer from cfDNA. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The number of neuroendocrine transformation cases, the reference standard used to define transformation, and whether the finding was validated are not stated. A single or few cases would not support a general detection claim. Why it matters This is the most clinically consequential claim in the abstract and is presented without any indication of cohort size or validation. Resolution test Report the number of transformation events, the reference standard (for example histopathology or clinical criteria), and independent validation, ideally with sensitivity and specificity. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Terminology precision Affected element Use of "define" in the title and abstract Evidence pointer Title; Abstract; location not provided Issue "Define" implies a causal or deterministic relationship that correlational cfChIP-seq data cannot establish. Required correction Soften to "are associated with" or "distinguish" unless causal evidence is provided. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Cohort reporting Affected element Patient and sample description Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue No sample sizes, cancer stages, treatment status, or cohort composition are given for the prostate cancer plasma cohort or the independent cfChIP-seq cohort. Required correction Add cohort sizes and key clinical characteristics in the abstract or main text. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Comparator description Affected element "state-of-the-art fragmentomics-based tumor fraction predictor" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The comparator is not named or cited, and the basis for the superiority claim is not specified. Required correction Name and cite the comparator and state the metric and conditions of comparison. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Numerical consistency Affected element Genome fraction of the 50-MAP panel Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The claim that the panel uses fragments from "< 0.001% of the genome" is not accompanied by the genomic span or calculation. Required correction Provide the panel footprint and how the percentage was computed. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Data and code availability Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue No accession numbers or code repository are mentioned. Required correction Provide data accessions and analysis code. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3 (blocking); R1-M4 and R1-M5 additionally required for the correlative and clinical claims respectively. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality Moderate to high if substantiated. Using histone-modification-associated nucleosome offsets in cfDNA as a readout is a distinct angle relative to standard fragmentomics, though it builds on established cfChIP-seq and nucleosome-positioning literature. Scientific importance Potentially high for liquid biopsy if the modification-specificity and TF-independence claims hold. Currently asserted rather than demonstrated in the supplied material. Interdisciplinary readership Reasonable. The work spans epigenetics, computational genomics, and oncology, which suits a broad audience if the technical basis is made accessible. Technical soundness Not assessable from the abstract. Specificity of cfChIP-seq, control for sequence and accessibility confounders, and held-out evaluation of the 50-MAP model are unresolved. Readability for nonspecialists The abstract is generally clear, but terms such as MAPs, cfChIP-seq, and tumor fraction are used without brief definition, and the distinction between correlation and causation is blurred by "define." Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. Supportive of further consideration only if the blocking technical concerns (R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3) are resolved with full methods, controls, and held-out validation. Risk / unsupported claims That histone modifications "define" nucleosome positions, which asserts causality not demonstrated by the supplied material (unsupported as stated). That the 35,120 MAPs are modification-associated, absent antibody validation and background controls (not assessable). That MAP protection reflects histone modification status differences between cancer and non-malignant chromatin, absent adjustment for fragmentomic confounders (weak as presented). That the 50-MAP model achieves AUC 0.91-0.96 and outperforms a state-of-the-art predictor, absent a described held-out evaluation and named comparator (not assessable). That MAP protection at ASCL1 sites identifies neuroendocrine transformation, absent cohort size, reference standard, and validation (not assessable). That the approach is a "mutation-independent readout of tumor fraction and cancer state from routine cfDNA sequencing," which generalizes beyond the evidence presented (overreach relative to supplied material).

Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract addresses a genuinely interesting and timely question in plant chromatin biology, namely how regulatory information is coordinated in the apparent absence of CTCF and strong compartmental domains. The three-layer model is conceptually clear and potentially useful as an organizing framework. However, from the supplied material alone, the manuscript reads as a synthesis and opinion piece whose central model is asserted rather than demonstrated. No specific evidence, no cited examples, and no mechanistic detail are visible, so the strength of the underlying support cannot be evaluated. The abstract is well written and accessible, but the case for the model remains unestablished from what is provided. The three-layer framework (histone marks, transcription factors, cohesin loops) is a clear and testable conceptual model. The abstract is concise and readable for a broad audience. The framing around a "global folding" strategy versus animal compartmentalization is a useful comparative angle. no figures, methods, or statistical details were available for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that partial (~50%) depletion of CTCF or RAD21 in an isogenic iPSC-to-iEC differentiation system causes EC-specific loss of CTCF and RAD21 promoter occupancy, that RAD21 reduction has a stronger effect on endothelial gene expression than CTCF depletion, and that RAD21 loss redistributes FLI1 binding genome-wide, implicating cohesin in the control of endothelial transcriptional programs. Visible evidence base CUT&Tag and RNA-seq data, as described in the abstract; no quantitative results, effect sizes, or statistical measures are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, all figures and tables, statistical analyses, genome-wide occupancy tracks, differential expression lists, and any validation experiments Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract addresses a genuine and under-explored question, namely how architectural proteins regulate transcription in terminally differentiated cells, using a controlled isogenic differentiation system. The experimental design, comparing partial depletion in iPSCs versus iECs, is conceptually strong and represents a meaningful advance over prior near-complete depletion studies. However, the abstract alone does not provide sufficient quantitative evidence to evaluate the robustness of the central claims. The EC-specificity of the observed effects, the differential impact of RAD21 versus CTCF depletion, and the proposed mechanistic link between cohesin reduction and FLI1 redistribution are all plausible but currently under-supported. The manuscript may be of interest to the chromatin and vascular biology communities, but the case is not fully established from the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying 3D genome organization, cohesin and CTCF biology, endothelial cell identity, and vascular gene regulation. The isogenic iPSC-to-iEC system will also appeal to those interested in differentiation-coupled chromatin changes. The FLI1 finding may attract investigators focused on endothelial transcription factor networks and vascular disease. Major strengths The use of partial depletion (~50%) in an isogenic differentiation system is a clear improvement over lethal near-complete knockout approaches. The comparison between undifferentiated and lineage-committed states directly addresses cell-type specificity. The focus on a terminally differentiated cell type fills a gap in a field dominated by proliferative systems. The identification of FLI1 redistribution as a potential downstream consequence of cohesin loss offers a novel mechanistic angle. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "RAD21 reduction had a more pronounced impact on endothelial gene expression than CTCF depletion" Evidence pointer RNA-seq, described in abstract; no quantitative data provided Concern The abstract states that RAD21 depletion has a greater effect on endothelial gene expression than CTCF depletion, but no effect sizes, numbers of differentially expressed genes, statistical thresholds, or replication details are provided. It is unclear whether this difference is quantitative (more genes affected), qualitative (different gene sets), or based on a specific metric. Why it matters This is a central comparative claim of the paper. Without quantitative support, the reader cannot assess whether the difference is biologically meaningful or within technical variation. Resolution test Provide the number of differentially expressed genes for each depletion, overlap statistics, effect size distributions, and appropriate statistical comparisons between the two conditions. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic support Claim pointer "RAD21 loss also led to a marked redistribution of FLI1 binding" Evidence pointer CUT&Tag, described in abstract; no genomic context or quantitation provided Concern The abstract claims that FLI1 binding is redistributed upon RAD21 loss, but does not specify the direction of redistribution (gained versus lost sites), the genomic features involved, or whether the changes are correlated with gene expression changes. The mechanistic link between cohesin reduction and FLI1 occupancy is asserted but not demonstrated. Why it matters The title and the concluding statement rest on this redistribution being a key mechanism. Without details on where FLI1 moves and whether this movement explains transcriptional changes, the mechanistic claim remains correlative. Resolution test Show the numbers of gained and lost FLI1 peaks, their genomic annotation, motif analysis, and integration with differentially expressed genes to establish a regulatory link. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Specificity of the effect Claim pointer "a striking, EC-specific loss of CTCF and RAD21 occupancy at gene promoters following partial depletion" Evidence pointer CUT&Tag, described in abstract; no comparison data shown Concern The claim of EC-specificity rests on the comparison between iPSCs and iECs, but the abstract does not report whether the same partial depletion was achieved in both cell types, whether occupancy changes were measured at matched loci, or whether the iPSC results were truly negative or simply weaker. Why it matters The EC-specificity is a central novelty claim. If occupancy loss also occurs in iPSCs but with different consequences, the interpretation shifts from cell-type-specific chromatin regulation to a more general phenomenon with cell-type-specific outcomes. Resolution test Provide quantitative occupancy changes in both cell types at shared and unique promoter loci, with statistical comparison of the depletion effect across cell states. Required correction Either temper the conclusion to reflect that chromatin architecture changes are inferred rather than directly assayed, or state explicitly if architectural measurements were performed. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3. The abstract does not provide sufficient quantitative or mechanistic evidence to support the three central claims of differential RAD21 versus CTCF effects, FLI1 redistribution, and EC-specificity. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: the question of architectural protein function in differentiated cells is timely and the partial-depletion approach is a genuine methodological improvement, but the conceptual framework is not entirely novel. Scientific importance: potentially high for vascular biology and chromatin fields, but the significance depends on the robustness of the EC-specificity and FLI1 findings, which cannot be evaluated from the abstract. Interdisciplinary readership: the work bridges genome organization, transcription factor biology, and endothelial biology, which should attract a broad audience if the evidence is strong. Technical soundness: the design is sound in principle, but the abstract does not demonstrate that the analyses are statistically robust or that the conclusions follow from the data. Readability for nonspecialists: the abstract is clearly written and accessible, though some terms (e.g., "CUT&Tag") may require context for a general audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The experimental approach is promising and the question is worthwhile, but the abstract alone does not provide sufficient quantitative or mechanistic support for the central claims. A full assessment requires the figures, methods, and statistical details. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that RAD21 depletion has a more pronounced effect on endothelial gene expression than CTCF depletion is unsupported without quantitative RNA-seq results. The claim that FLI1 binding is redistributed upon RAD21 loss is unsupported without peak-level data and genomic context. The claim of EC-specificity of occupancy loss is unsupported without direct comparison of quantitative changes in iPSCs versus iECs. The mechanistic conclusion that cohesin controls vascular programs through coordinated chromatin architecture and transcription factor occupancy is not established, as chromatin architecture was not directly demonstrated in the abstract.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Heterochromatin protein 1alpha acts as an essential stabilizer of chromatin packing domains 作者 ：Kuo, Tiffany; Carrillo Gonzalez, Paola; Acosta, Nicolas; Carter, Lucas M; Pujadas Liwag, Emily; Arriaga, Claudia V; Johnson, Brittany; Dunton, Cody L; Almassalha, Luay M; Szleifer, Igal; Backman, Vadim 单位 ：未提供（根据作者名单推测为 Northwestern University 相关团队，但原文未明确标注） 期刊/平台 ：bioRxiv（预印本服务器） 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：预印本（preprint），未经同行评审 领域 ：染色质结构、表观遗传学、基因组组织、转录调控 关键词 ：chromatin packing domains, HP1alpha, heterochromatin, loop extrusion, transcription, hypoxia DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.10.05.753292 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（未提及数据可用性声明） 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14（按当前日期推算） 在「cpdch基因家族」方向中的位置 ：本文不直接涉及 cpdch 基因家族，但研究对象为染色质 packing domain（CPD）的结构稳定化机制，核心因子为 HP1alpha（CBX5 编码蛋白）。对于 cpdch 基因家族研究，本文提供了 CPD 形成的分子机制框架、HP1alpha 作为 CPD 稳定因子的证据，以及 CPD 结构-转录功能关系的定量分析方法，可作为 cpdch 基因产物在染色质结构调控中功能研究的参照体系。 02 一句话总结 本文通过短期降解 HP1alpha 结合染色质成像与转录组分析，证明 HP1alpha 的染色质交联作用是 packing domain 成熟（heterochromatic core 形成）的必要条件，其缺失破坏 domain 几何结构并抑制缺氧应激下的转录重编程。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：HP1alpha 在染色质 packing domain 的成熟和稳定中扮演什么角色？其缺失如何影响 domain 结构及转录功能？ 为什么重要 ：packing domain 是 50-200 nm 尺度的染色质基本结构单元，其组织方式与转录调控密切相关。理解 HP1alpha 在 domain 成熟中的作用，有助于阐明异染色质如何通过结构机制而非简单的可及性抑制来调控基因表达。 现有方法为何不足 ：传统观点认为异染色质通过限制染色质可及性来抑制转录，但该框架无法解释为何 HP1alpha 缺失导致整体转录下调（而非上调）。此外，多数研究关注 HP1alpha 在端粒、着丝粒等特定异染色质位点的功能，缺乏对其在全基因组 packing domain 结构中作用的系统分析。 精确研究问题 ：Can short-term HP1alpha degradation disrupt the heterochromatic cores of dense packing domains and thereby impair transcriptionally responsive chromatin remodeling under stress? 04 背景与发展脉络 脉络标注 ：以下脉络基于本文引言及参考文献框架，未经外部系统核验，标注为「仅本文框架」。 阶段一：染色质层级结构的发现 。Hi-C 等技术揭示了染色质折叠为 TAD、compartment 等层级结构。代表性方法：Hi-C、Micro-C。优点：提供全基因组接触图谱；局限：分辨率不足以解析 50-200 nm 的 packing domain 结构。 阶段二：packing domain 的提出与表征 。Backman 团队利用超分辨率光学成像（如 STORM）发现染色质存在 50-200 nm 的 packing domain，具有 mass-scaling 行为。优点：直接观测纳米尺度的染色质密度分布；局限：通量低，难以覆盖全基因组。 阶段三：domain 形成机制的探索 。研究发现 nascent domain 通过转录和 cohesin/CTCF 介导的 loop extrusion 形成，而 domain 成熟依赖于表观遗传酶对核心（高密度）与外周（低密度）的差异可及性，导致 heterochromatic marks 在核心积累。优点：将结构形成与生化过程联系起来；局限：对成熟过程中关键交联因子的作用缺乏直接实验证据。 阶段四（本文位置） ：本文提出 HP1alpha 作为 H3K9me3 的 reader 和染色质交联因子，是 domain 成熟的关键稳定剂。通过急性降解系统直接检验 HP1alpha 缺失对 domain 结构和转录的影响，填补了 domain 成熟机制中「交联因子如何稳定核心结构」的空白。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 异染色质功能悖论 HP1alpha 缺失导致整体转录下调，而非预期中的去抑制 作者解释：HP1alpha 交联维持 domain 核心结构，为外周形成「ideal zone」提供结构基础；核心破坏导致外周转录支持区域丧失 Results 节（转录组数据） domain 核心结构脆弱性 短期 HP1alpha 降解即导致 dense domain 的 heterochromatic core 破坏 作者解释：HP1alpha 对 H3K9me3 的交联是核心密度维持的直接物理机制 Results 节（染色质成像数据） 应激响应失效 HP1alpha 缺失细胞在缺氧条件下转录响应减弱 作者解释：domain 成熟被破坏后，染色质无法有效重编程以响应环境信号 Results 节（缺氧实验） 结构-功能因果方向不清 传统模型认为可及性决定转录，但无法解释 HP1alpha 缺失的下调效应 作者解释：packing domain 通过非单调密度-转录关系（ideal zone）支持转录，而非简单可及性 引言及 Discussion 节 06 核心思想 1. 表面方法 ：使用急性降解系统（如 auxin-inducible degron，推测）快速耗尽 HP1alpha，结合超分辨率染色质成像（STORM 或类似技术）定量分析 packing domain 的密度分布和 mass-scaling 行为，同时进行 RNA-seq 检测转录变化，并在缺氧条件下测试应激响应能力。 2. 核心洞察 ：HP1alpha 不仅是转录抑制因子，更是 packing domain 核心结构的「物理稳定剂」。其交联作用维持 domain 核心的高密度状态，而核心的存在通过非单调密度-转录关系在外周创造转录最适的「ideal zone」。因此，HP1alpha 缺失不是「打开」染色质促进转录，而是「破坏」结构导致转录支持功能丧失。 3. 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：基因调控因子的功能不能仅从其生化活性（如抑制、激活）推断，必须放在染色质层级结构的物理框架中理解。一个「抑制性」因子可能通过维持结构完整性来间接支持转录。这一思路可迁移到 cpdch 基因家族研究：若 cpdch 基因产物参与染色质结构调控，其功能可能同样具有结构-转录的双向关系，而非简单的激活/抑制。 07 方法总览 输入 ：人类细胞系（具体类型未提供，推测为上皮或成纤维细胞系）；HP1alpha 急性降解系统；缺氧处理条件。 输出 ：packing domain 结构参数（密度分布、mass-scaling 指数、核心完整性）、转录组变化、应激响应基因表达谱。 模块 ： 1. abstract; no methods, figures, or statistical details were available for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose that HP1alpha acts as an essential stabilizer of chromatin packing domains, that its short-term degradation disrupts heterochromatic domain cores while paradoxically causing global transcriptional downregulation, and that HP1alpha-depleted cells show a dampened transcriptional response to hypoxia. They conclude that HP1alpha crosslinking is essential for domain maturation and that this relationship between chromatin architecture and gene regulation could inform chromatin engineering-based treatments. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, experimental methods, statistical analyses, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting and counterintuitive finding regarding HP1alpha function in chromatin packing domain maintenance and transcriptional regulation. The central observation that HP1alpha degradation leads to transcriptional downregulation rather than upregulation is intriguing and could challenge simple models of heterochromatin-mediated repression. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient methodological detail and quantitative evidence to evaluate the robustness of the claims. The mechanistic link between domain geometry disruption and transcriptional outcomes remains correlative rather than causal in the presented narrative. The work may be of interest to the chromatin biology and genome architecture communities, but the current evidence base is too limited to assess whether the conclusions are fully supported. Who would be interested in the results, and why Chromatin biologists studying heterochromatin function and genome organization; researchers in the 3D genome field interested in packing domain architecture; investigators studying transcriptional regulation under stress conditions; those working on chromatin engineering approaches for therapeutic applications. The paradoxical transcriptional phenotype and the hypoxia response findings would be of particular interest to these groups. Major strengths The central finding is counterintuitive and potentially important, as it challenges the canonical view that heterochromatin removal should increase transcriptional accessibility. The use of short-term degradation (implying a degron system) is a methodologically sound approach for acute protein depletion. The hypoxia perturbation provides a functional readout that connects domain architecture to physiological responses. The conceptual framing linking packing domain maturation to differential enzyme access is a useful theoretical contribution. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "HP1alpha loss disrupts domain geometry and inhibits efficient transcriptional reprogramming" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract states that HP1alpha degradation disrupts heterochromatic cores of dense packing domains and that some packing domains persisted, but no quantitative data are presented on the extent, specificity, or statistical significance of these structural changes. The claim that domain geometry disruption leads to inhibited transcriptional reprogramming implies a causal relationship, but the abstract does not establish whether the transcriptional defects are a direct consequence of domain disruption or an independent effect of HP1alpha loss on other chromatin functions. Why it matters The central conclusion of the paper rests on linking structural changes in packing domains to functional transcriptional outcomes. Without quantitative evidence for the degree of domain disruption and without experiments distinguishing direct from indirect effects, the causal chain remains unsubstantiated. Resolution test Provide quantitative measurements of domain size, density, and core integrity before and after HP1alpha degradation, with appropriate statistical comparisons. Include experiments that separate the structural effects of HP1alpha loss from its biochemical functions, such as rescue experiments with HP1alpha mutants that can crosslink but not bind H3K9me3, or vice versa. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic interpretation Claim pointer "short-term HP1alpha degradation resulted in overall downregulation of genes, contrasting with the canonical view that repression of heterochromatin allows chromatin to become more accessible for transcription" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract reports global transcriptional downregulation upon HP1alpha loss but provides no information on the magnitude, gene class specificity, or temporal dynamics of this effect. The interpretation that this is paradoxical assumes that HP1alpha loss should primarily de-repress heterochromatic genes, but HP1alpha has multiple functions beyond H3K9me3 binding, including roles in DNA repair, replication, and telomere maintenance. The abstract does not address whether the observed downregulation could be a secondary consequence of genome instability or other HP1alpha functions. Why it matters The "paradoxical" framing is a key selling point of the paper. If the downregulation is explained by known non-repressive functions of HP1alpha, the finding is less surprising and the interpretation shifts substantially. The mechanistic interpretation must account for the full range of HP1alpha functions. Resolution test Provide RNA-seq data showing the distribution of up- and downregulated genes, their chromatin states, and their genomic features. Include experiments addressing whether the transcriptional changes correlate with DNA damage, replication stress, or other HP1alpha-dependent processes. Compare the transcriptional response to HP1alpha loss with that of H3K9me3 loss or SUV39 inhibition to isolate the contribution of the HP1alpha-H3K9me3 axis. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Functional relevance Claim pointer "when domain maturation is disrupted, stress response pathways are not effectively activated" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The hypoxia experiment is presented as evidence that HP1alpha depletion dampens stress-responsive transcription, but the abstract does not specify which genes or pathways were examined, how many were affected, or whether the effect is specific to hypoxia-responsive genes or reflects a general impairment of transcription. The claim that this demonstrates a failure of "effective activation" requires knowing whether the baseline transcriptional defect in HP1alpha-depleted cells confounds the interpretation of the hypoxia response. Why it matters The hypoxia result is used to argue for the physiological relevance of packing domain architecture. If the dampened response is simply a reflection of globally reduced transcription, the specific link to domain maturation is weakened. Resolution test Show that hypoxia-responsive genes are specifically and disproportionately affected relative to the global transcriptional changes. Include time-course data demonstrating that the failure is in activation kinetics rather than steady-state levels. Provide evidence that the affected genes are specifically localized to domains whose architecture is disrupted by HP1alpha loss. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Terminology clarity Affected element "essential stabilizer" in title and conclusions Evidence pointer Title and abstract Issue The term "essential stabilizer" implies an absolute requirement, but the abstract states that "some packing domains persisted" after HP1alpha degradation, suggesting partial redundancy or context-dependence. The title may overstate the essentiality. Required correction Consider qualifying the claim, such as "critical stabilizer" or specifying the conditions under which HP1alpha is essential, or provide evidence that all domains are affected to justify "essential." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Conceptual framing Affected element "ideal zone" concept Evidence pointer Background section Issue The "ideal zone" concept is introduced in the background but its relationship to the HP1alpha findings is not explicitly articulated in the results or conclusions. It is unclear whether the hypoxia data specifically test this model or whether the model is merely contextual. Required correction Explicitly connect the "ideal zone" model to the experimental findings, or state that the current work does not directly test this model. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope of conclusions Affected element "could inform chromatin engineering-based treatments" Evidence pointer Conclusions Issue The therapeutic implication is stated without any evidence that the findings have translational relevance. This is speculative and not supported by the data described in the abstract. Required correction Either remove the therapeutic speculation or clearly label it as speculation beyond the current findings. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are the primary technical concerns. The causal link between domain disruption and transcriptional outcomes must be established with appropriate controls and quantitative data. The interpretation of the transcriptional phenotype must account for the multifunctional nature of HP1alpha. Without these, the central claims of the paper are not established from the provided evidence. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The paradoxical transcriptional phenotype is potentially original and could challenge existing models. However, the abstract does not provide enough context to assess how novel this is relative to existing literature on HP1alpha and heterochromatin function. Scientific importance: If the causal link between packing domain architecture and transcriptional reprogramming is rigorously established, this would be an important contribution to understanding how genome structure relates to function. The current evidence is suggestive but not conclusive. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges chromatin biology, biophysics, and gene regulation, which could appeal to a broad readership. The abstract is written in a way that is largely accessible, though some specialized terminology may limit accessibility. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. The methods for domain measurement, degradation efficiency, and transcriptional analysis are not described. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is reasonably clear but relies on specialized concepts (packing domains, mass-scaling behavior, H3K9me3) that may be challenging for readers outside the chromatin field. The logical flow from background to results to conclusions is coherent. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents an intriguing hypothesis and preliminary findings, but the absence of methodological detail, quantitative data, and controls prevents assessment of whether the claims are supported. The work has potential merit and warrants full review of the complete manuscript, but the case as presented in the abstract is not yet convincing. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that HP1alpha is an "essential stabilizer" of packing domains is not supported by the abstract, which acknowledges that some domains persist after HP1alpha loss. The causal claim that domain disruption "inhibits efficient transcriptional reprogramming" is not established; the abstract does not rule out alternative explanations for the dampened hypoxia response. The therapeutic implication ("could inform chromatin engineering-based treatments") is entirely speculative and unsupported by any data in the abstract. The "ideal zone" model is presented as established background but its relationship to the current findings is not articulated. The paradoxical nature of the transcriptional downregulation is asserted but not contextualized against the full range of HP1alpha functions beyond H3K9me3 binding.

abstract; no figures, methods, or supplementary materials were provided for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that alcohol exposure displaces elongating RNAPIIs2p from gene bodies to promoters and to guanine-rich intergenic CTCF sites. They further claim that high guanine content at the CTCF motif ZF5 binding position predicts increased CTCF and cohesin (RAD21) occupancy, that these changes persist six days after alcohol withdrawal, that Hi-C reveals no impact on structural CTCF loops but altered enhancer-promoter contacts with lasting gene expression changes, and that the same sequence rule applies in a mouse starvation model and in placentae after paternal alcohol exposure. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or statistical details provided Missing materials affecting confidence All primary data, experimental methods, statistical analyses, genome-wide datasets, and validation details; the abstract references findings across multiple model systems without any supporting data visible Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting hypothesis-driven study linking sequence-specific guanine content in CTCF motifs to alcohol-induced chromatin redistribution. The central idea, that acetaldehyde's guanine-directed chemistry produces sequence-dependent rather than stochastic chromatin changes, is mechanistically plausible and conceptually appealing. However, the abstract compresses a large amount of work across multiple model systems into a very small space, and the absence of any supporting data makes it impossible to evaluate the robustness of the claims. The persistence claim (six days post-withdrawal) and the cross-model generalizability claims are particularly strong and would require substantial evidence. The disconnect between CTCF/cohesin changes and structural loop stability, with effects instead on enhancer-promoter contacts, is an interesting and somewhat counterintuitive finding that would benefit from clearer mechanistic explanation. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying alcohol's molecular effects on chromatin and gene expression; investigators in the CTCF/cohesin and 3D genome organization field; those interested in sequence-dependent mechanisms of environmentally induced epigenetic changes; and potentially researchers studying transgenerational effects of alcohol exposure, given the paternal exposure finding. Major strengths The hypothesis is mechanistically grounded in acetaldehyde's known guanine-directed chemistry, providing a clear sequence-dependence rationale. The study spans multiple levels of analysis, from transcription factor occupancy to 3D genome organization to gene expression, and extends beyond a single cell-line model to two in vivo contexts. The persistence finding, if well-supported, would have significant implications for understanding lasting effects of alcohol exposure. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "CTCF occupancy changes persisting even six days after alcohol withdrawal" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract claims that CTCF occupancy changes persist for six days after alcohol withdrawal, which is a strong temporal claim. No information is provided about the experimental design supporting this, including the time course sampled, the number of biological replicates, the magnitude of the persistent changes relative to acute changes, or whether this persistence is specific to certain loci. Why it matters This persistence claim is central to the paper's significance, as it suggests lasting molecular consequences of alcohol exposure. If the effect decays substantially over the six-day period or is only significant at a subset of loci, the interpretation would change considerably. The claim also implies a mechanism for maintaining altered occupancy after the initial insult is removed, which is not addressed. Resolution test Provide the full time-course data showing CTCF occupancy at multiple time points post-withdrawal, with statistical comparisons at each time point, and demonstrate that the persistence is robust across replicates and not driven by a small number of outlier loci. These are substantial claims that imply the sequence rule is generalizable across different stressors and across generations. No details are provided about the experimental design, sample sizes, the magnitude of effects, or how "the same sequence rule" was tested in these contexts. Why it matters These cross-model claims significantly broaden the paper's scope and implications. If the rule applies across different stressors and in a transgenerational context, this would suggest a general principle of sequence-dependent chromatin vulnerability. However, the abstract provides no evidence that these models were tested with equivalent rigor, and the paternal exposure finding in particular raises complex questions about mechanism that are not addressed. Resolution test Provide detailed methods and results for each model system, including sample sizes, statistical power, effect sizes, and explicit demonstration that the guanine-content rule predicts occupancy changes in each context. This is a surprising finding that challenges simple models of CTCF function in loop maintenance. The abstract does not explain how CTCF and cohesin occupancy can change substantially without affecting loops, nor how enhancer-promoter contacts are altered independently. Why it matters This is arguably the most mechanistically interesting and potentially controversial finding in the paper. If CTCF occupancy changes do not affect structural loops, the field's understanding of CTCF's role in loop maintenance would need revision, or the authors need to provide an alternative explanation for why loops are stable despite occupancy changes. The mechanism linking altered enhancer-promoter contacts to lasting gene expression changes is also unclear.
