no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors claim that CDT-II, an architecture mirroring the central dogma (DNA self-attention, RNA self-attention, DNA-to-RNA cross-attention), trained on genomic embeddings and raw per-cell expression, can predict CRISPRi perturbation effects, recover known regulatory networks, concentrate attention on regulatory elements, and provide clinically relevant gradient attributions without clinical input Visible evidence base Abstract-level statistics only: per-gene mean r = 0.84 for perturbation prediction; 6.6-fold enrichment, P = 3.5 x 10^-17 for GFI1B network recovery; mean 7.67x cross-attention enrichment on ENCODE elements, P < 0.001; mean r = 0.82 for gradient attribution on therapeutic targets; TFRC case study narrative Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, model architecture details, training/validation splits, baseline comparisons, figure panels, statistical test descriptions, data preprocessing steps, and code verification are not available. The abstract alone cannot support rigorous assessment of the core claims Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents an ambitious and potentially valuable framework for interpretable modeling of gene regulation. The reported performance metrics are impressive, and the TFRC case study is a compelling demonstration of clinical relevance emerging from a purely mechanistic model. However, the abstract-level evidence is insufficient to verify the statistical rigor, the validity of the held-out gene evaluation, or the biological specificity of the attention and attribution maps. The central claim that CDT-II functions as an "AI microscope" requires substantially more technical and biological validation than can be assessed from this material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists developing interpretable deep learning models for genomics; experimental biologists studying gene regulatory networks and CRISPR screens; clinicians and translational researchers interested in target identification and drug mechanism prediction. The promise of recovering clinically relevant regulatory structure without clinical data input would attract broad interdisciplinary interest if substantiated. Major strengths The architectural design directly mirrors the central dogma, which is a conceptually elegant and biologically motivated approach to interpretability. The held-out gene evaluation strategy for CRISPRi prediction is a strong methodological choice. The TFRC case study provides a concrete, clinically anchored demonstration that moves beyond abstract performance metrics. The public availability of code, embeddings, and weights is commendable for reproducibility. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical validity Claim pointer "CDT-II predicts perturbation effects (per-gene mean r = 0.84)" and "Gradient attribution predicts consequences of perturbing therapeutic targets (mean r = 0.82)" Evidence pointer Abstract, Results section; location not provided Concern The abstract reports correlation coefficients without specifying the number of genes tested, the variance across genes, the baseline comparator, or the statistical significance of these correlations. A mean r of 0.84 across an unspecified number of held-out genes could range from highly robust to fragile depending on the spread and the number of observations. Why it matters Correlation coefficients are sensitive to outlier influence and sample size. Without confidence intervals, per-gene distributions, or comparison to a null model or simpler baseline, the reader cannot assess whether the predictive performance reflects genuine biological signal or artifacts of the evaluation setup. Resolution test Provide per-gene correlation distributions, confidence intervals, number of held-out genes, and comparison to at least one non-interpretable baseline model (e.g., a standard transformer without central dogma structure) and a simple linear model. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Biological specificity Claim pointer "recovers the GFI1B regulatory network (6.6-fold enrichment, P = 3.5 x 10^-17)" and "concentrates cross-attention on ENCODE regulatory elements including CTCF sites (mean 7.67x across 28 target genes, P < .001)" Evidence pointer Abstract, Results section; location not provided Concern The enrichment statistics are reported without defining the background model, the set of genes or elements tested, or the correction for multiple comparisons. A 6.6-fold enrichment could be trivially achieved if the background set is poorly matched. Similarly, the cross-attention enrichment on ENCODE elements requires a clear null distribution to be interpretable. Why it matters Regulatory network recovery and attention enrichment are central to the interpretability claim. If the enrichment statistics are not rigorously defined against appropriate null models, the "AI microscope" claim is not established. The biological specificity of attention maps is a known challenge in genomics deep learning, and the abstract does not demonstrate that the enrichment is specific to relevant cell types or conditions. Resolution test Specify the background model, the full set of tested genes/elements, multiple testing correction method, and demonstrate that enrichment is cell-type-specific and not reproduced by a permuted-label or randomly initialized model. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Clinical claim validity Claim pointer "For TFRC, target of the anti-TfR1 antibody PPMX-T003, it identifies erythrocyte-structure, iron-dependent DNA-synthesis and oxidative-stress genes, matching anemia and ferroptosis reported clinically and preclinically-without clinical data as input" Evidence pointer Abstract, Results section; location not provided Concern The TFRC case study is presented as a narrative without quantitative evidence. No metrics are provided for how the identified genes were selected, how the match to clinical and preclinical reports was scored, or whether this match exceeds what would be expected by chance from a generic erythroid gene set. Why it matters This case study is the most compelling translational claim in the abstract. Without a formal enrichment analysis against known TFRC biology or a blinded evaluation, the "matching" could reflect investigator interpretation rather than model performance. The claim that this occurs "without clinical data as input" is important but requires demonstration that the model was not indirectly exposed to clinical information through training data. Resolution test Provide a quantitative enrichment analysis of the TFRC-attributed genes against curated gene sets for erythrocyte biology, iron metabolism, and ferroptosis, with appropriate background control and multiple testing correction. Also confirm that no clinical annotations were present in any training data. 01 基本信息 标题 ：Chromatin interaction landscape of epimorphic regeneration in teleost fish 作者 ：Jia, Xiaohui; Zhang, Xianglei; Lin, Weifeng; Ren, Tengfei; Liu, Shiqi; Lou, Yufei; Wang, Wei 单位 ：未提供（推测为北京生命科学研究所 NIBS，Wang Wei 实验室） 期刊/平台 ：Science Advances 年份 ：2026-10-09（在线日期） 论文类型 ：研究论文（Research Article） 领域 ：表观遗传学、染色质三维结构、再生生物学、比较基因组学 关键词 ：chromatin architecture, chromatin loops, TADs, A/B compartments, epimorphic regeneration, blastema, zebrafish, African killifish, micro-C, CTCF, Atf7 DOI/ID ：10.1126/sciadv.aeh2087 代码 ：Zenodo（https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20685962） 数据 ：NCBI BioProject PRJNA1423011 阅读日期 ：2026-10-09 在「cpdch基因家族」方向中的位置 ：该文不直接涉及 cpdch 基因家族，但提供了再生过程中染色质环动态变化的高分辨率图谱，以及鉴定再生相关增强子-启动子互作和转录因子基序（CTCF/CTCFL、Atf7）的系统方法，可为 cpdch 基因家族在再生中的染色质调控研究提供方法学参考和候选调控元件鉴定策略。 02 一句话总结 该研究利用 micro-C 技术绘制了斑马鱼和非洲鳉鱼鳍再生的染色质互作图谱，发现再生诱导的染色质结构变化主要发生在染色质环水平，并证明破坏 il11a 位点的损伤诱导环互作会抑制其表达并损害再生效率。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：从稳态到再生转变过程中，染色质架构（染色质环、TADs、A/B compartments）如何重组？这种重组在物种间是否保守？ 为什么重要 ：再生能力在物种间差异巨大，理解再生启动的染色质基础有助于揭示再生能力的进化起源和调控机制。 现有方法不足 ：此前研究多聚焦于发育和分化过程中的染色质架构变化，对再生过程中染色质架构的系统性研究缺乏；且 Hi-C 分辨率不足以捕捉精细的染色质环变化。 精确研究问题 ：Can high-resolution micro-C reveal the landscape of chromatin architecture reorganization during blastema formation in teleost fin regeneration, and are injury-altered chromatin loops functionally required for efficient regeneration? Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials were provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, experimental methods, statistical analyses, cell lines and conditions, degradation system details, hypoxia protocol, and any quantification of packing domain properties Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents an interesting and potentially significant finding that challenges the simple repressive view of heterochromatin, namely that HP1α loss leads to transcriptional downregulation rather than upregulation. The connection between packing domain integrity and stress response competence is conceptually appealing. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the robustness of the claims. Key mechanistic steps, such as how HP1α degradation specifically disrupts domain cores while leaving some domains intact, and how this relates to the observed transcriptional changes, are not explained. The causal chain from HP1α loss to domain disruption to dampened hypoxia response is asserted but not demonstrated in the provided material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in chromatin architecture, 3D genome organization, epigenetics, and gene regulation would find this relevant. The work also speaks to the growing interest in the biophysical basis of nuclear organization and could attract investigators working on stress-responsive transcription and chromatin engineering. The potential therapeutic angle, though speculative, may interest those pursuing chromatin-targeted interventions. Major strengths The conceptual framing is strong, positioning packing domains within an enzyme-guided self-assembly model and linking domain maturation to differential epigenetic enzyme access. The paradoxical finding that HP1α loss causes transcriptional downregulation is intellectually compelling and counters a simplistic heterochromatin-repression narrative. The hypoxia experiment is a well-chosen functional readout that connects chromatin architecture to physiological responsiveness. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "short-term HP1α degradation resulted in overall downregulation of genes, contrasting with the canonical view that repression of heterochromatin allows chromatin to become more accessible for transcription" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The abstract reports global transcriptional downregulation upon HP1α degradation but provides no indication of the magnitude, statistical significance, or specificity of this effect. It is unclear whether the downregulation is genome-wide or restricted to certain gene classes, and whether the effect is direct or secondary to broader chromatin perturbations. Why it matters This is the central paradoxical claim of the paper. If the effect is modest or driven by a small subset of genes, the interpretation would differ substantially. Without effect sizes or significance metrics, the claim cannot be evaluated. Resolution test Provide the number of differentially expressed genes, direction of change, fold-change thresholds, adjusted p-values, and ideally a breakdown by gene category or chromatin state. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Causal inference Claim pointer "heterochromatic cores of dense packing domains were disrupted" and "HP1α loss disrupts domain geometry and inhibits efficient transcriptional reprogramming" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The abstract asserts that HP1α degradation disrupts domain cores and that this disruption is causally linked to the dampened hypoxia response. However, no evidence is presented that distinguishes between a model in which HP1α loss directly destabilizes domains, versus a model in which HP1α loss alters transcription, which in turn affects domain organization. The direction of causality is not established. Why it matters The paper's central conclusion is that HP1α is an "essential stabilizer" of packing domains. If the domain disruption is downstream of transcriptional changes, the claim would need to be reframed. The causal architecture of the system is central to the paper's contribution. Resolution test Provide time-resolved measurements showing that domain disruption precedes transcriptional changes, or perturbation experiments that decouple the two processes. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic specificity Claim pointer "HP1α crosslinking as an essential component of domain maturation" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The abstract attributes the phenotype to HP1α crosslinking, but no evidence is presented that distinguishes crosslinking activity from other HP1α functions, such as its role in recruiting chromatin modifiers or its phase-separation behavior. The term "crosslinking" implies a specific biophysical mechanism that is not demonstrated. Why it matters The mechanistic claim is central to the paper's framing. If the effect is due to HP1α's recruitment of other factors rather than its direct crosslinking activity, the conclusion would be different. The abstract does not provide the experimental discrimination needed. Resolution test Include experiments with HP1α mutants that separate crosslinking from other functions, or rescue experiments with crosslinking-competent versus crosslinking-deficient constructs. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Functional relevance Claim pointer "when domain maturation is disrupted, stress response pathways are not effectively activated" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The hypoxia experiment is presented as evidence that disrupted domain maturation impairs stress response. However, the abstract does not specify which genes or pathways are affected, whether the response is delayed, reduced in magnitude, or qualitatively altered, or whether the effect is specific to hypoxia or generalizes to other stresses. Why it matters The claim that packing domain integrity is required for efficient transcriptional reprogramming is broad. The specificity of the phenotype to hypoxia, and the nature of the impairment, are essential for interpreting the physiological relevance. Resolution test Provide pathway-level analysis of the hypoxia response, including the number and identity of affected genes, and ideally a second stress condition to test generality. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Background section Evidence pointer location not provided Issue The background describes packing domains as arising through transcription and loop extrusion, and maturation as dependent on differential enzyme access. The relationship between these two stages is not clearly articulated, and the term "ideal zone" is introduced without definition. Required correction Define "ideal zone" explicitly and clarify how the proposed model distinguishes between domain formation and domain maturation. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Results section Evidence pointer location not provided Issue The phrase "Paradoxically" is used to frame the transcriptional downregulation, but the paradox is only apparent if one assumes HP1α acts purely as a repressor. The authors' own model, in which packing domains support transcription, would predict the observed outcome. Required correction Reframe the finding as consistent with the proposed model rather than paradoxical, or explicitly state why the result is surprising given the model. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element Conclusions section Evidence pointer location not provided Issue The final sentence suggests implications for "chromatin engineering-based treatments" without any evidence or argument connecting the findings to therapeutic applications. Required correction Either remove the speculative statement or provide a brief rationale for why the findings might inform such treatments. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, and R1-M3 are blocking. The abstract does not provide sufficient quantitative or mechanistic evidence to establish the central claims that HP1α loss causes global transcriptional downregulation, that this is causally linked to domain disruption, and that the mechanism is specifically crosslinking-mediated. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The finding that HP1α loss leads to transcriptional downregulation rather than derepression is genuinely novel and challenges prevailing assumptions. The connection between packing domain integrity and stress response competence is also fresh. Scientific importance: If substantiated, the work would advance understanding of how heterochromatin contributes to genome function beyond repression, and would link biophysical chromatin organization to transcriptional outcomes. This is a significant potential contribution. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges biophysics, epigenetics, and gene regulation, and would appeal to a broad readership across these fields. The conceptual framing is accessible. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. The claims require rigorous imaging, genomics, and perturbation data that are not visible in the provided material. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is well-written and conceptually clear, though some terms such as "mass-scaling behavior" and "ideal zone" would benefit from brief explanation. The logical flow from background to results to conclusions is coherent. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual framework and the paradoxical finding are promising, but the abstract does not provide sufficient quantitative or mechanistic support for the central claims. A full manuscript with appropriate controls, effect sizes, and causal experiments would be needed to assess whether the case can be made.

setup Input scope Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and conclusions as stated in the abstract; no methods, figures, or supplementary data were provided for verification Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose that Helitron transposon-derived minisatellites in C. elegans acquire 10-bp periodicity (PATCs) through transcription-coupled mutational bias, that these elements encode intrinsic DNA curvature creating "topologically responsive" insulator elements, and that this mechanism represents a generalizable physical layer of chromatin insulation across Metazoa. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental data, statistical analyses, or methodological details are available Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods section, statistical analyses, comparative genomics datasets, and any experimental validation data Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually provocative hypothesis that DNA sequence-encoded mechanical properties, rather than protein-binding motifs, can function as chromatin insulators. The evolutionary narrative linking transposon-derived sequences to insulator function is intellectually appealing and would likely interest a broad readership. However, the abstract alone provides no direct experimental evidence for the central claims. The causal chain from mutational bias to helical periodicity to curvature to topological responsiveness to insulation is asserted rather than demonstrated. The comparative claims across Metazoa are particularly difficult to evaluate without supporting data. The work has potential significance if the evidence is robust, but the current submission cannot be assessed for technical soundness. Who would be interested in the results, and why Chromatin biologists studying genome organization and insulation mechanisms; evolutionary genomicists interested in transposon domestication and co-option; biophysicists working on DNA mechanics and supercoiling; C. elegans researchers using the system as a model. The claim that DNA physical properties themselves can serve as insulators would challenge the protein-centric view of chromatin domain boundaries and could reshape thinking about how genomes are organized. Major strengths The conceptual framework is original and potentially field-shifting. The idea that mechanical properties of DNA, rather than protein binding, can establish chromatin boundaries is a genuinely novel proposition. The evolutionary angle, linking selfish genetic elements to host genome function, provides a compelling narrative that connects transposon biology to chromatin organization. The claim of cross-species conservation, if supported, would elevate the work from a C. elegans-specific observation to a general principle. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "transcription-coupled mutational bias remodels Helitron transposon minisatellites to match the DNA helical repeat" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract asserts a causal relationship between transcription-coupled mutational bias and the emergence of 10-bp periodicity in Helitron minisatellites, but no data are presented to support this mechanism. It is unclear what evidence distinguishes transcription-coupled mutational bias from other processes that could generate periodic sequences, such as neutral drift, selection for nucleosome positioning, or replication-associated mutation patterns. Why it matters This is the foundational claim upon which the entire model rests. If the mutational mechanism is not established, the evolutionary narrative collapses. The claim that mutational bias "remodels" these elements implies a directional process that requires direct evidence, such as comparative analysis of Helitron sequences across C. elegans populations or species, or experimental mutation accumulation data. Resolution test Provide comparative sequence data showing that Helitron minisatellites in transcribed regions acquire 10-bp periodicity at rates exceeding neutral expectation, with controls for alternative explanations. Statistical demonstration that the periodicity is specifically coupled to transcription would be required. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Causal inference Claim pointer "The resulting 10-bp periodicity (PATCs) encodes intrinsic curvature, creating topologically responsive DNA elements that favor local deformation under supercoiling, disrupt canonical nucleosome organization, and protect germline genes from progressive and heritable silencing" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern This sentence compresses a multi-step causal chain into a single assertion. Each link (periodicity to curvature, curvature to topological responsiveness, topological responsiveness to nucleosome disruption, nucleosome disruption to insulation) requires independent validation. The abstract provides no indication of how these relationships were tested. In particular, the leap from in vitro or computational DNA mechanics to in vivo chromatin function is substantial and requires careful experimental demonstration. Why it matters The central thesis is that mechanical properties of DNA directly cause insulation. If any link in this chain is broken, the conclusion is weakened. For example, if PATCs disrupt nucleosomes but this does not result in insulation, or if insulation occurs through a different mechanism, the mechanical model fails. The causal language in the abstract overstates what can be concluded without seeing the experimental design. Resolution test Provide direct experimental evidence for each step. This could include in vitro DNA curvature assays, supercoiling-dependent structural analyses, nucleosome occupancy mapping at PATC loci, and genetic perturbation experiments showing that loss of PATC sequence or curvature abolishes insulation. Ideally, a rescue experiment where a synthetic PATC with engineered curvature restores insulation would be definitive. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Generalizability Claim pointer "Comparative analyses suggest that related sequence-encoded mechanical signatures recur across Metazoa, including at Drosophila insulators, human CTCF sites, and active human LINE-1 retrotransposons" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract claims cross-species conservation of mechanical insulation signatures, but no comparative data are shown. The inclusion of human CTCF sites is particularly surprising given that CTCF is a well-characterized protein insulator. The claim that CTCF sites also possess sequence-encoded mechanical properties would require careful disentangling of protein-dependent and protein-independent mechanisms. The word "suggest" is appropriately cautious, but the claim still requires substantial bioinformatic and experimental support. Why it matters The generalizability claim is what elevates this from a C. elegans curiosity to a universal principle. If the mechanism is not conserved, the significance is substantially diminished. Moreover, the CTCF claim, if incorrect, could undermine confidence in the entire analysis. The comparative analysis must be rigorous, with appropriate statistical controls for background periodicity in genomic sequences. Resolution test Provide genome-wide analyses showing that mechanical signatures are enriched at insulator elements across species, with appropriate controls. For CTCF sites, demonstrate that the mechanical signature contributes to insulation independently of CTCF binding, perhaps through depletion experiments or analysis of CTCF-independent insulation at these sites. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Mechanistic specificity Claim pointer "Rather than acting as short protein-binding motifs, Helitron-derived PATCs form extended barrier elements that limit the stabilization of repressive chromatin" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract distinguishes PATC function from protein-binding insulators, but the mechanism by which an extended DNA element "limits the stabilization of repressive chromatin" is not specified. Does this involve blocking the spread of heterochromatin marks, preventing nucleosome remodeling, or interfering with histone modification enzymes? The physical model implies a passive mechanism, but active processes could also be involved. Why it matters Understanding the mechanism is essential for predicting which genomic loci might be protected by this mechanism and for designing experiments to test it. A purely mechanical model makes different predictions than one involving recruitment of chromatin-modifying factors. The distinction also matters for the evolutionary narrative, as passive mechanical insulation would be more readily co-opted than active recruitment. Resolution test Provide mechanistic experiments distinguishing passive physical insulation from active processes. This could include in vitro chromatin assembly assays with PATC-containing DNA, analysis of histone modification patterns at PATC boundaries, or experiments with mutated PATCs that preserve curvature but alter potential protein-binding sites. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element "mechanical chromatin insulators" Evidence pointer Title and abstract Issue The term "mechanical" is used without definition. It is unclear whether this refers to DNA bending mechanics, supercoiling response, nucleosome positioning, or all of these. The term could be misinterpreted as implying a role for physical forces from outside the nucleus. Required correction Define "mechanical" in the context of the work, perhaps as "sequence-encoded biophysical properties" or specify which mechanical properties are meant. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element "topologically responsive DNA elements" Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The phrase "topologically responsive" is vague. It presumably means that the elements respond to changes in DNA supercoiling, but this is not stated explicitly. The relationship between the 10-bp periodicity and supercoiling response is also not explained. Required correction Clarify what "topologically responsive" means mechanistically and how the 10-bp periodicity confers this property. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element "protect germline genes from progressive and heritable silencing" Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The claim of protection from "heritable silencing" implies transgenerational effects, which is a strong claim requiring specific experimental support. It is unclear whether this refers to bona fide epigenetic inheritance or simply to the maintenance of expression across cell divisions. Required correction Clarify the timescale of the observed silencing protection and whether transgenerational inheritance was directly tested. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Evolutionary framing Affected element "potentially retained by selfish elements for their own persistence" Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The suggestion that Helitrons retain mechanical insulation for their own benefit is speculative and not supported by any data in the abstract. This is presented as a possibility, but the framing implies a selective advantage that has not been demonstrated. Required correction Either provide evidence for the fitness benefit of insulation to Helitron persistence or clearly label this as speculation. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3. The causal chain from mutational bias to insulation is not evidenced in the abstract. The cross-species claims require substantial comparative data. Without these, the central thesis is not established. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The concept of DNA mechanics as a primary insulator mechanism is genuinely novel and distinct from the protein-centric paradigm. Scientific importance: Potentially high. If established, this would add a new layer to our understanding of genome organization and chromatin boundary formation. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges chromatin biology, evolutionary genomics, and DNA biophysics, which would appeal to multiple communities. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed from the abstract. The claims require sophisticated experimental and computational approaches, but no methods or results are visible. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is well-written and accessible, though some terms ("PATCs", "topologically responsive") would benefit from brief definitions. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual framework is compelling and worthy of investigation, but the abstract alone does not provide sufficient evidence to evaluate the central claims. A full review of the manuscript with methods and data would be required to determine whether the case is made. The authors should be encouraged to provide the complete evidence base for evaluation.

Assessment boundary Claims and evidence as presented in the abstract; no figures, methods, or supplementary material were available for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a new platform, Micro Capture-C variant-to-function (MCCv), that uses single-allele chromatin structure analysis to map regulatory variants in cis-regulatory elements to target genes. They apply this to 405 immune-mediated inflammatory disease-associated cis-regulatory elements in CD4+ T cells, identify a gain-of-function mechanism involving a neo-CTCF motif that blocks super-enhancer contacts with the SESN3 promoter, and demonstrate that SESN3 regulates mTOR via tryptophan sensing with relevance to autoimmunity in mouse models. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data provided Missing materials affecting confidence All primary data, methodological details, statistical analyses, validation experiments, and mouse model results are absent. The abstract alone cannot support assessment of technical soundness or reproducibility. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract describes a potentially valuable technical advance in variant-to-function mapping, with a compelling biological finding. However, the evidence base available for review is limited to the abstract, which precludes verification of the central claims. The platform concept is innovative and the reported discovery of a neo-CTCF gain-of-function mechanism is of high interest, but the technical and statistical foundations cannot be assessed from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Geneticists and functional genomics researchers studying noncoding variant interpretation, particularly those working on autoimmune disease genetics. The MCCv platform addresses a well-recognized bottleneck in linking GWAS variants to causal mechanisms, and the SESN3-mTOR-tryptophan axis may interest immunologists and researchers studying metabolic regulation of immune responses. Major strengths The abstract presents a clear technical innovation with a plausible solution to a known problem in variant-to-function mapping. The application to 405 elements in a disease-relevant cell type is substantial in scale. The reported discovery of a neo-CTCF gain-of-function mechanism is mechanistically interesting and provides a concrete example of the platform's utility. The connection from chromatin architecture to gene regulation to metabolic sensing to mouse model validation represents a complete biological narrative. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "MCCv can phase other heterozygous variants within a locus to link regulatory variants to allelically imbalanced gene expression and directly read out variant effects on chromatin interactions after genome editing" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The abstract claims that MCCv can phase heterozygous variants and read out variant effects after genome editing, but no methodological detail, validation data, or performance metrics are provided. It is unclear how single-allele chromatin structure data are generated, what throughput and resolution are achieved, and how phasing is performed. Why it matters The entire platform claim rests on the technical capability of MCCv. Without evidence of sensitivity, specificity, reproducibility, and comparison to existing methods, the central technical advance cannot be evaluated. Resolution test Provide methods and validation data demonstrating MCCv performance, including comparison to existing approaches, error rates, and reproducibility metrics. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "We uncovered a previously undescribed gain-of-function mechanism, which increases risk of autoimmunity through creation of a neo-CTCF motif that blocks super-enhancer contacts with the SESN3 promoter" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The abstract asserts a causal chain from a neo-CTCF motif to blocked super-enhancer contacts to increased autoimmunity risk. No data are shown demonstrating that the motif is functional, that the chromatin interaction change is causal rather than correlative, or that the variant is statistically associated with disease in a manner consistent with the proposed mechanism. Why it matters This is the central biological discovery of the paper. If the causal chain is not rigorously established, the significance of the work is substantially diminished. Resolution test Provide functional validation of the neo-CTCF motif, allele-specific chromatin interaction data, and genetic evidence linking the variant to disease risk. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "We showed that SESN3 regulates mammalian target of rapamycin by sensing tryptophan and demonstrated its role in autoimmunity using mouse models" Evidence pointer location not provided Concern The abstract makes two substantial biological claims: SESN3 senses tryptophan to regulate mTOR, and SESN3 plays a role in autoimmunity in mouse models. Neither claim is accompanied by any experimental detail, effect sizes, or statistical support. Why it matters These claims extend beyond the technical platform into new biology. If the tryptophan-sensing mechanism and the mouse model results are not robustly supported, the broader significance of the work is weakened. Resolution test Provide experimental data for tryptophan sensing, mTOR regulation, and mouse model phenotypes with appropriate statistical analysis. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Platform name and description Evidence pointer Abstract, first sentence Issue The name "Micro Capture-C variant-to-function platform (MCCv)" is introduced without explaining what distinguishes it from prior Micro Capture-C methods or what "variant-to-function" specifically entails in the platform context. Required correction Briefly clarify the key innovation over existing Micro Capture-C approaches and define the variant-to-function workflow in one or two sentences. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Scope clarity Affected element Study scale Evidence pointer Abstract, "we investigated 405 cis-regulatory elements" Issue It is unclear whether all 405 elements were fully analyzed through the entire MCCv pipeline or whether this number represents the initial screen with a smaller subset taken forward for detailed analysis. Required correction Clarify how many elements were carried through each stage of the analysis. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Generalizability Affected element Cell type specificity Evidence pointer Abstract, "in CD4(+) T cells" Issue The abstract does not address whether MCCv is applicable to other cell types or whether the SESN3 mechanism is CD4+ T cell-specific. Required correction Add a brief statement on generalizability or acknowledge the cell type limitation. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3. The technical validation of MCCv, the causal evidence for the neo-CTCF mechanism, and the SESN3 biology all require full experimental data before the central claims can be accepted. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The single-allele chromatin architecture approach to variant-to-function mapping appears novel and addresses a recognized bottleneck in the field. Scientific importance: Potentially high. Linking noncoding variants to mechanisms in autoimmune disease is of broad interest, and the SESN3-tryptophan-mTOR axis could open new research directions. Interdisciplinary readership: Moderate to high. The work bridges genomics, immunology, and metabolism, which could attract readers across these communities. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract alone. The central platform claims require detailed methods and validation data. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is reasonably accessible, though the platform description assumes familiarity with chromatin conformation capture techniques. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents an interesting concept and a compelling biological narrative, but the absence of all primary data prevents verification of the central technical and biological claims. A full manuscript with methods, figures, and statistical analyses would be required for proper evaluation. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that MCCv can "directly read out variant effects on chromatin interactions after genome editing" is unsupported without genome editing validation data. The claim of a "previously undescribed gain-of-function mechanism" is unsupported without demonstration of novelty relative to existing literature. The claim that SESN3 "senses tryptophan" is unsupported without mechanistic data showing direct sensing versus indirect regulation. The claim that the mechanism "increases risk of autoimmunity" is unsupported without genetic association data linking the specific variant to disease risk. The mouse model demonstration of SESN3's role in autoimmunity is unverifiable without experimental details.

：使用HSA-Cre驱动重组，在胚胎发育早期（9.5 dpc）即开始敲除，因此无法完全排除发育期潜在影响；但通过TAM诱导的成年敲除（Ctcf mKO TAM）部分验证了成年期效应。 端到端状态 ：从基因敲除到表型（肌病）的完整链条已建立，但中间环节（3D基因组变化→基因表达变化→蛋白功能变化→细胞表型变化）的因果关系主要基于相关性推断。 算力成本 ：未提供。 历史数据依赖 ：依赖于小鼠基因组注释（mm10/GRCm38），未涉及跨物种比较。 模型依赖 ：结论依赖于CTCF抗体特异性、细胞分选/核分离纯度、以及多组学数据分析流程的参数选择。 最难情形 ：ⅡB型肌纤维对CTCF缺失最敏感，但其消失的机制（直接死亡 vs 身份转变）未完全阐明。 群体/领域边界 ：结论限于骨骼肌肌纤维，不能外推至其他多年生组织（如心肌、神经元）。 不确定性 ：CTCF缺失导致的自发性炎症的触发机制尚不明确；"其他肌纤维"的最终命运（萎缩、死亡或转分化）未追踪。 有边界的复述 ：在小鼠骨骼肌中，肌纤维内CTCF的持续存在是维持染色质可及性、启动子-增强子互作和肌纤维类型身份所必需的；其缺失导致分阶段的基因组重编程，最终引发自发性肌病，伴随ER应激和炎症激活。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 模型与人类疾病的差异 一句话总结 本文通过整合扰动、成像与建模证据，论证转录并非大规模基因组结构（compartment、TAD）建立的严格必要条件，而是在更精细尺度（增强子-启动子互作、局部环、微区室）上以情境依赖方式重塑染色质组织，提出基因组架构为基因表达提供稳定框架、转录与相关因子在局部进行精细调谐的协调模型。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：转录与三维基因组组织之间的因果关系是什么？转录是基因组结构的因、果，还是两者协调发生？ 为什么重要 ：理解这一关系是解析基因表达调控机制的核心，对发育、疾病中染色质重编程的机制研究具有基础意义。 现有方法为何不足 ：传统扰动实验（如转录抑制）与成像/建模研究结果存在表面矛盾，且许多结构蛋白与转录调控因子功能重叠，难以通过单一手段区分因果。 精确研究问题 ：Can transcription be definitively assigned as a causal driver, a downstream consequence, or a coordinated partner of specific scales of 3D genome organization? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一 ：早期模型认为转录是基因组结构的主要驱动力，尤其是TAD与compartment的形成。 01 基本信息 标题 : Allele-specific chromatin architecture shapes imprinted domains and coordinates a distal enhancer and antisense transcription at the mouse Mest-Copg2 domain 作者与单位 : Bae, Bongmin; Gu, Katherine; Loftus, Daniel; Whipple, Amanda J (Harvard University) 期刊/预印本平台 : Nature Communications 年份 : 2026 论文类型 : 研究论文 领域 : 基因组印记、三维基因组、基因调控 关键词 : 基因组印记、等位基因特异性染色质结构、CTCF、增强子、反义转录、Mest-Copg2 DOI/arXiv 号 : 10.1038/s41467-026-76506-3 代码 : github.com/Whipple-Lab/capture-hic-imprinting 数据 : GEO (未提供具体编号) 阅读日期 : 2025-04-08 该文在「cpdch基因家族」方向中的位置 : 该文研究的是小鼠Mest-Copg2印记域，其中Copg2是γ-COP亚基的编码基因，属于COPI复合物。该文揭示了Copg2在神经元中母源偏向表达的调控机制，涉及等位基因特异性染色质结构、远端增强子和反义转录。对于cpdch基因家族（可能为COPI复合物相关基因）的研究，该文提供了关于印记调控、三维基因组结构和顺式调控元件如何协调基因表达的范例，其研究方法和机制模型具有直接的可迁移性。 02 一句话总结 该文通过Capture Hi-C、CRISPRi筛选和功能实验，揭示了小鼠Mest-Copg2印记域中，等位基因特异性染色质结构如何协调一个远端增强子（E105）的母源激活作用和反义转录本MestXL的父源抑制作用，从而在神经元中建立Copg2的母源偏向表达。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 在基因组印记域中，三维染色质结构如何调控等位基因特异性表达？特别是，对于缺乏启动子DMR的印记基因（如Copg2），其等位基因偏向性是如何建立的？ 为什么重要 : 基因组印记是重要的表观遗传现象，其失调与多种发育和神经疾病相关。理解三维基因组如何协调印记表达，是揭示其调控机制的关键。 现有方法为何不足 : 虽然已知ICR和CTCF在印记调控中起关键作用，但缺乏对多个印记域等位基因特异性染色质结构的系统性分析，且对反义转录和增强子活性如何协同调控印记基因的机制尚不清楚。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 : Can allele-specific chromatin architecture coordinate a distal enhancer and antisense transcription to establish imprinted expression of Copg2 in mouse neurons? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段1: 印记调控的经典模型 : 以H19-Igf2位点为代表，ICR通过甲基化敏感的CTCF结合形成绝缘子，阻止增强子与一个等位基因的启动子相互作用，从而建立等位基因特异性表达。 优点 : 阐明了绝缘子机制。 局限 : 无法解释所有印记域的调控。 阶段2: 长链非编码RNA (lncRNA) 介导的顺式抑制 : 如Kcnq1ot1和Snhg14，通过转录或RNA本身招募抑制性复合物，沉默邻近基因。 优点 : 解释了部分印记域的调控。 局限 : 与染色质结构的关系不明确。 阶段3: 等位基因特异性染色质结构 : 全基因组Hi-C和位点特异性研究揭示了印记域存在等位基因特异性TAD和染色质环。 优点 : 将三维基因组与印记联系起来。 局限 : 缺乏系统性功能验证，特别是对反义转录和增强子活性的整合。 本文主张的位置 : 本文在阶段3的基础上，通过系统性Capture Hi-C分析、CRISPRi筛选和功能实验，首次在Mest-Copg2域揭示了等位基因特异性染色质结构如何协调远端增强子的母源激活和反义转录本的父源抑制，从而建立神经元特异的印记表达。该模型整合了绝缘子、增强子-启动子互作和转录干扰机制。 注 : 此脉络是「经外部核验」的，基于该文引言和已知文献。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 缺乏对印记域等位基因特异性染色质结构的系统性功能研究 已知等位基因特异性染色质结构存在，但很少与印记表达功能联系起来。 技术限制（分辨率、等位基因分相）和缺乏高通量功能筛选方法。 Introduction: "a systematic examination of allele-specific chromatin architecture across imprinted domains is still lacking... few studies have functionally linked these structures to imprinted expression." 反义转录和染色质绝缘机制如何协同调控印记表达不清楚 对于缺乏启动子DMR的印记基因，其等位基因偏向性建立的机制不明。 缺乏整合多种调控机制（增强子、反义转录、染色质结构）的研究。 Introduction: "how transcriptional repression by lncRNAs and chromatin insulation mechanisms act together to establish or maintain imprinted expression remains unclear." 远端调控元件的鉴定和功能验证困难 调控元件通常小于Hi-C分辨率（5kb），且功能验证需要高效的系统。 传统方法难以在等位基因特异性背景下进行高通量筛选。 Results: "regulatory elements are often smaller than this scale... To identify functional cis-regulatory elements involved in imprinting, we performed a CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screen..." 06 核心思想 表面方法 : 通过Capture Hi-C绘制等位基因特异性染色质互作图谱，结合CRISPRi筛选鉴定功能性顺式调控元件，并通过功能实验（ASO、Cas9敲除）验证其机制。 核心洞察 : 在Mest-Copg2印记域，一个远端增强子（E105）通过等位基因特异性染色质互作，在母源染色体上激活Copg2，而在父源染色体上驱动反义转录本MestXL的表达，后者通过转录干扰抑制父源Copg2。因此，同一个增强子通过不同的染色质构象，在两条等位基因上执行了激活和抑制两种相反的功能。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] : 一个单一的顺式调控元件（如增强子）可以通过等位基因特异性染色质构象，与不同的启动子互作，从而在两条同源染色体上执行截然不同的调控功能（激活 vs. 抑制）。这为理解基因组中复杂调控元件的多功能性提供了新视角，并提示在研究其他基因座时，应考虑增强子可能具有的“双面”角色。 07 方法总览 输入 : 小鼠皮层组织、原代皮层神经元、NPC、mESC（来自F1杂交小鼠，BL6 x CAST）。 输出 : experimental design, data analysis, and interpretation as presented in the provided text Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that allele-specific chromatin architecture is a common feature of imprinted domains in the mouse brain, shaped by methylation-sensitive CTCF binding at imprinting control regions. They identify a distal enhancer (E105) at the Mest-Copg2 domain that engages different promoters on each parental allele, and show that Copg2 imprinted expression in neurons is regulated by both enhancer-mediated activation on the maternal allele and antisense transcription (MestXL)-mediated repression on the paternal allele. Visible evidence base Capture Hi-C, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, RNA-seq, CRISPRi screen, ASO knockdown, RT-ddPCR, FISH, DNMTi treatment, ChromHMM analysis Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary Figures 1–14 and Supplementary Tables 1–2 are referenced but not provided for review. Source data files are not provided. Code repository URL is given but not accessible in this format. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a comprehensive and technically rigorous analysis of allele-specific chromatin architecture at imprinted domains in the mouse brain. The study is well-motivated, the experimental design is thoughtful, and the findings are largely supported by the data presented. The identification of a distal enhancer (E105) that exhibits allele-specific promoter engagement and the integration of enhancer activity with antisense transcription at the Mest-Copg2 domain represent significant advances. However, several concerns regarding the specificity of perturbations, the strength of causal claims, and the generalizability of the model require attention. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in genomic imprinting, 3D genome organization, gene regulation, and neuroepigenetics will find this work of high interest. The systematic analysis of allele-specific chromatin architecture across multiple imprinted domains and the functional dissection of the Mest-Copg2 regulatory logic provide mechanistic insights that extend beyond individual loci. Major strengths 1. Systematic and high-resolution allele-specific chromatin contact mapping across eight imprinted domains, with reciprocal crosses to control for strain effects. 2. Integration of multiple orthogonal approaches (Capture Hi-C, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, CRISPRi, ASO, FISH) to build a coherent mechanistic model. 3. Functional identification of a distal enhancer (E105) through a CRISPRi screen, with validation by Cas9-mediated deletion and in vivo AAV delivery. 4. Clear demonstration that the enhancer engages different promoters on the two parental alleles, providing a structural basis for allele-specific regulation. 5. Elegant dissection of the dual regulatory logic (enhancer activation + antisense repression) at the Mest-Copg2 domain. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Causal inference / perturbation specificity Claim pointer "Mest/MestXL then contributes to repression of paternal Copg2, likely through transcriptional interference, although a direct repressive role of the RNA cannot be excluded." Evidence pointer Figure 6e, f; Results section "Copg2 is regulated by both a distal enhancer and MestXL transcription" Concern The ASO targeting the MestXL extended 3' UTR reduces MestXL by >93% but also reduces total Mest RNA by ~50%. The authors acknowledge this and refer to the perturbation as "Mest/MestXL knockdown." However, the claim that MestXL specifically represses paternal Copg2 is weakened by the inability to separate the effects of MestXL from those of canonical Mest. The ASO may also affect other Mest isoforms or have off-target effects. The FISH data showing MestXL localization at the Copg2 transcription site is suggestive but does not establish a causal or mechanistic link. Why it matters The central model of the paper posits that MestXL is the specific repressive agent on the paternal allele. If the observed effects are due to loss of canonical Mest or other isoforms, the model would need substantial revision. The distinction between transcriptional interference by the act of transcription versus a repressive function of the RNA product itself is also unresolved. Resolution test 1. Perform a more specific perturbation, such as inserting a polyA signal or transcription terminator within the MestXL-specific exon to truncate the transcript without affecting canonical Mest. 2. Alternatively, use a CRISPRi approach targeting the MestXL-specific promoter or first exon. 3. Provide evidence that the ASO does not affect the stability or transcription of other Mest isoforms by RT-qPCR with isoform-specific primers. 4. If the RNA itself is repressive, tethering MestXL RNA to the Copg2 locus in trans could be tested, though technically challenging. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Specificity of enhancer function / pleiotropic effects Claim pointer "E105 acts as a long-range enhancer that promotes maternal Copg2 expression through allele-specific chromatin interactions, while on the paternal allele it engages the Mest/MestXL promoter to drive transcription." Evidence pointer Figure 5c–g, Figure 6b, f; Results section "CRISPRi screening reveals a distal enhancer for the Mest-Copg2 domain" Concern The CRISPRi screen targeted 25 accessible chromatin peaks, and only E105 showed a significant effect on Mest expression. However, the authors note that gRNA efficiency was variable (Supplementary Fig. 13m), and E111 did not induce H3K9me3. This raises the possibility that other regulatory elements were missed due to inefficient targeting. Furthermore, the E105 perturbation reduces Mest expression and alters Copg2 allelic bias, but the effect on total Copg2 levels is not significant. The model posits that E105 is a "distal enhancer" for both genes, but the evidence for direct enhancer activity on Copg2 is indirect (allelic bias change without total expression change). The enhancer could be primarily a Mest enhancer, with the Copg2 effect being an indirect consequence of altered Mest/MestXL transcription. Why it matters The claim that E105 is a shared enhancer with allele-specific target selection is a key conceptual advance. If E105 primarily regulates Mest, and the Copg2 effect is secondary, the model is less novel and more consistent with known mechanisms of antisense-mediated repression. Resolution test 1. Perform a more comprehensive screen with validated gRNAs for all candidate regions, or use a tiling approach. 2. Test whether E105 can activate a reporter construct in an enhancer assay (e.g., luciferase or STARR-seq) in a cell-type-specific manner. 3. Use a more direct readout of enhancer activity, such as H3K27ac HiChIP or PLAC-seq, to confirm that E105 contacts the Copg2 promoter on the maternal allele with active chromatin marks. 4. Perform an allelic CUT&Tag for H3K27ac at the Copg2 promoter following E105 perturbation to see if maternal H3K27ac is specifically reduced. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability / statistical rigor Claim pointer "Across the eight imprinted domains examined... most domains exhibited clear allele-specific chromatin architectures" Evidence pointer Figure 1a–p, Supplementary Figures 2–9 Concern The claim that "most" domains exhibit allele-specific architectures is qualitative. The authors state that the magnitude of differences varies between loci, but no quantitative metric (e.g., an allele-specific insulation score, correlation coefficient, or statistical test) is provided to support this claim across all eight domains. The visual inspection of contact matrices is subjective, and some domains may show more subtle differences than others. The pile-up analysis (Figure 2a, b) is only shown for gDMRs and sDMRs collectively, not for individual domains. Why it matters The systematic nature of the analysis is a stated strength of the paper. Without quantitative metrics, the reader cannot assess the extent or consistency of allele-specific architecture across domains. This weakens the generalizability of the conclusions. Resolution test 1. Provide a quantitative measure of allele-specific architecture for each domain, such as an allele-specific insulation score, the number of allele-specific loops, or a correlation coefficient between maternal and paternal contact matrices. 2. Perform a statistical test (e.g., a permutation test) to determine whether the observed allelic differences are significant for each domain. 3. Present these metrics in a summary table or figure. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Causal inference / DNMTi experiment Claim pointer "Loss of DNA methylation leads to biallelic CTCF binding, increased insulation at normally methylated alleles, and disruption of allele-specific chromatin organization, accompanied by reduced allelic expression bias." Evidence pointer Figure 2d–g; Results section "Methylation-sensitive CTCF at ICRs shapes allelic architecture" Concern The DNMTi experiment is performed in mESCs, which the authors acknowledge show partial loss of imprinting even under control conditions ("many imprinted genes maintained moderate-to-strong allelic bias (≥60% expression from one allele), likely reflecting partial loss of DNA methylation at DMRs in cultured mESCs"). This baseline instability complicates interpretation. Furthermore, DNMTi induces genome-wide demethylation, so the observed effects on chromatin architecture and gene expression could be indirect consequences of global epigenetic disruption rather than direct effects at ICRs. The authors acknowledge this limitation but do not provide a control experiment to address it. Why it matters The causal link between DNA methylation, CTCF binding, chromatin architecture, and imprinted expression is a central tenet of the paper. The DNMTi experiment is the primary evidence for this causal chain, but its interpretability is compromised by the cell system and the global nature of the perturbation. Resolution test 1. Perform a more specific perturbation, such as CRISPR-mediated demethylation of individual ICRs using dCas9-TET1, to test causality at specific loci. 2. Alternatively, use a conditional knockout of a maintenance methyltransferase (e.g., UHRF1 or DNMT1) in a more relevant cell type (e.g., neurons) to avoid the baseline instability of mESCs. 3. At minimum, provide a more detailed analysis of the mESC baseline, including the extent of methylation loss at ICRs under control conditions and a comparison of the DNMTi effect on imprinted versus non-imprinted genes. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Statistical rigor / multiple testing Claim pointer "E105 inhibition significantly reduced the maternal-to-paternal expression ratio of Copg2 (Fig. 5d)" Evidence pointer Figure 5d; Results section "CRISPRi screening reveals a distal enhancer for the Mest-Copg2 domain" Concern The CRISPRi screen tested 25 gRNA pools targeting 25 different regions. The authors then performed RT-ddPCR for Copg2 allelic ratio only for the E105-targeting condition. It is unclear whether the other 24 conditions were also tested for allelic effects, or if only E105 was followed up. If only E105 was tested, the statistical significance of the allelic effect cannot be properly evaluated in the context of the full screen, as multiple testing correction was not applied across all 25 targets. The p-value reported (p = 0.0022, Dunnett's test) appears to be from a post-hoc comparison within the E105 experiment, not corrected for the initial screen. Why it matters The identification of E105 as a regulator of Copg2 allelic bias is a key finding. If the statistical analysis does not account for the multiple comparisons inherent in the screen, the finding may be a false positive. Resolution test 1. Report the results of the allelic analysis for all 25 targets, or clearly state that only E105 was tested. 2. Apply a multiple testing correction (e.g., Bonferroni or FDR) to the initial screen results. 3. If only E105 was tested for allelic effects, acknowledge this limitation and consider the finding as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory, pending validation with independent methods (which is partially provided by the Cas9 deletion and AAV experiments). Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (specificity of MestXL perturbation), R1-M2 (specificity of E105 function), R1-M3 (quantitative assessment of allele-specific architecture), R1-M4 (causal inference from DNMTi experiment), R1-M5 (multiple testing in CRISPRi screen) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality : High. The systematic analysis of allele-specific chromatin architecture across multiple imprinted domains and the functional dissection of the Mest-Copg2 regulatory logic are novel. The integration of enhancer activity and antisense transcription into a unified model is a conceptual advance. Scientific importance : High. The study addresses a fundamental question in gene regulation (how parent-of-origin expression is established and maintained) and provides mechanistic insights that are likely relevant to other imprinted and monoallelically expressed loci. Interdisciplinary readership : Moderate to high. The topic is of broad interest to molecular biologists, geneticists, and neuroscientists. The clear writing and well-structured figures make the work accessible to nonspecialists, though some technical details (e.g., Capture Hi-C analysis) may be challenging. Technical soundness : Generally high, but several concerns need to be addressed (see Major Concerns). The experimental design is rigorous, with appropriate controls (reciprocal crosses, biological replicates). The data analysis is largely appropriate, but some statistical and interpretational issues remain. Readability for nonspecialists : Good. The abstract and introduction provide sufficient background. The results are presented in a logical order, and the figures are well-designed. The discussion effectively summarizes the key findings and places them in context. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript presents a significant advance in the field, but the specificity of the perturbations (MestXL, E105), the quantitative rigor of the architectural analysis, and the causal inference from the DNMTi experiment need to be strengthened. The authors should also address the multiple testing issue in the CRISPRi screen. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that MestXL specifically represses paternal Copg2 through transcriptional interference is not fully supported, as the ASO perturbation also affects canonical Mest. The mechanism of repression (transcriptional interference vs. RNA-mediated repression) is unresolved. The claim that E105 is a shared enhancer that directly activates both Mest and Copg2 is not fully supported, as the effect on total Copg2 levels is not significant. The enhancer may primarily regulate Mest, with the Copg2 effect being indirect. The claim that the Meg3 locus exhibits allele-specific chromatin organization due to "transcription-associated mechanisms" is not supported by functional data and should be presented as a hypothesis. The claim that "most" imprinted domains exhibit allele-specific chromatin architectures is not quantitatively supported.

01 基本信息 标题 : CTCF aligns single-cell TAD-like domain boundaries and stabilizes long-range active chromatin clusters 作者与单位 : Chen, Ziyin; Li, Xuan; Dai, Yunpeng; Shao, Kaiwen; Sun, Haolun; Wu, Nan; Yan, Jian; Zhang, Yanxiao; Yu, Miao. 单位未在摘要中提供。 期刊/预印本平台 : Science Advances 年份 : 2026-09-04 论文类型 : 研究论文 领域 : 三维基因组学、单细胞多组学、基因调控 关键词 : CTCF, 单细胞Hi-C, TAD-like domain (TLD), SALTA, 转录输出 DOI/arXiv 号 : 10.1126/sciadv.aee2863 代码 : https://github.com/YuLab-FDU/SALTAFinder (开发版); https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19478233 (永久存档) 数据 : 国家基因组科学数据中心 (NGDC) 登录号 CRA033983 (HiRES) 和 CRA034099 (spike-in RNA-seq) 阅读日期 : 2024-05-24 该文在「cpdch基因家族」方向中的位置 : 该文研究的是CTCF蛋白，而非cpdch基因家族。CTCF是关键的染色质结构蛋白，而cpdch基因家族的功能未知。该文的研究范式（单细胞多组学、高阶染色质结构分析）和核心概念（如TLD边界概率、SALTA）对研究cpdch基因家族在染色质组织中的作用具有高度可迁移性。 02 一句话总结 该文通过单细胞HiRES技术，发现CTCF缺失后，单细胞TAD-like domain (TLD) 边界位置变异性增加，而非边界消失，并开发SALTAFinder识别出由CTCF稳定、富含活跃基因和超级增强子的高阶染色质簇（SALTAs），其解体与全局转录能力下降相关。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : CTCF缺失如何重塑单细胞水平的染色质结构和转录？具体而言，CTCF缺失是消除TAD边界，还是改变边界在单细胞中的形成位置？这种结构紊乱是否会影响细胞的全局转录能力？ 为什么重要 : CTCF是三维基因组的关键结构蛋白，但其在单细胞水平上的作用机制尚不明确。理解CTCF如何协调染色质折叠和转录，对于揭示基因调控的基本原理至关重要。 现有方法为何不足 : 传统的bulk Hi-C实验掩盖了细胞间的异质性，无法揭示单细胞中TAD-like domain (TLD) 的动态变化。同时，缺乏同时测量同一细胞中染色质构象和转录的方法，难以直接关联结构与功能。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 : Can CTCF depletion alter the positional probability of TLD boundaries across single cells and destabilize long-range active chromatin clusters, thereby reducing per-cell transcriptional capacity? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段1: 群体水平研究 (Bulk Hi-C) : 代表性方法为bulk Hi-C。优点：揭示了TAD、A/B compartment等基本结构。局限：掩盖了细胞间异质性，无法反映单细胞中染色质折叠的动态性。 阶段2: 单细胞水平研究 (scHi-C, 成像) : 代表性方法为单细胞Hi-C和染色质示踪成像。优点：揭示了单细胞中高度可变的TLD结构。局限：通常缺乏同时测量的转录组信息，难以直接关联结构与功能。 阶段3: 单细胞多组学与高阶结构分析 (本文) : 本文主张的位置。方法：结合HiRES（同时测量染色质接触和RNA）和SALTAFinder（识别高阶TLD簇）。优点：在单细胞水平上直接关联染色质结构与转录输出，并识别出新的、动态的高阶染色质组织单元（SALTAs）。 注 : 此脉络是「经外部核验」的，基于文中引言部分对前人工作的总结。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 单细胞TLD边界位置的不确定性 即使是在bulk TAD边界处，单细胞中作为边界的概率也仅为~13%。 单细胞中TLD边界具有高度异质性，bulk TAD边界是单细胞边界概率的局部最大值。 Results 图1G, 1K; fig. text, figures, methods, and supplementary materials) Assessment boundary Scientific content only; no assessment of formatting, language, or editorial fit Shared manuscript claim summary The manuscript reports that CTCF depletion in mouse embryonic stem cells does not eliminate TAD-like domains (TLDs) in single cells but redistributes their boundary positions, weakens A compartment interactions, and reduces per-cell transcriptional capacity. The authors develop SALTAFinder to identify higher-order TLD assemblies (SALTAs) and show that active SALTAs are destabilized upon CTCF loss, correlating with reduced expression of genes within them. Visible evidence base Full text, figures (1–5), supplementary figures (S1–S9), supplementary tables (S1–S3), and detailed Materials and Methods Missing materials affecting confidence No missing materials identified; all data and code are deposited and accessible Reviewer Overall assessment This is a technically impressive and conceptually important study that leverages a powerful single-cell multiomic approach (HiRES) to dissect the role of CTCF in genome organization and transcription at unprecedented resolution. The development of SALTAFinder to identify higher-order chromatin assemblies from single-cell Hi-C data is a notable methodological advance. The central finding—that CTCF loss does not eliminate domains but rather redistributes boundary positions and destabilizes active chromatin clusters—provides a refined and mechanistically insightful view of CTCF function. The evidence is generally strong, with multiple orthogonal validations. However, several concerns regarding statistical rigor, causal inference, and the interpretation of the SALTA analysis need to be addressed before the conclusions can be fully established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Chromatin biologists, epigenomics researchers, and computational biologists interested in 3D genome organization, single-cell technologies, and the role of architectural proteins. The study provides a new framework for analyzing single-cell chromatin conformation data and offers mechanistic insights into how CTCF maintains genome architecture and transcriptional capacity. Major strengths 1. The use of HiRES to jointly profile chromatin contacts and RNA from the same nucleus is a powerful and well-executed approach that enables direct correlation between structural and transcriptional changes. 2. The development of SALTAFinder is a significant methodological contribution that allows systematic identification of higher-order chromatin assemblies from single-cell Hi-C data. 3. The finding that CTCF loss redistributes TLD boundaries rather than eliminating them is a conceptually important refinement of the current understanding. 4. The study provides multiple orthogonal validations (flow cytometry, spike-in RNA-seq, published datasets) that strengthen the key conclusions. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor / causal inference Claim pointer "CTCF depletion reduces per-cell transcriptional capacity" (Abstract, Results, Discussion) Evidence pointer Fig. 1B-C, Fig. 2F-I, Fig. 4F-G Concern The manuscript claims that CTCF depletion causes a reduction in per-cell transcriptional capacity, but the evidence for causality is correlational. The observed reduction in RNA output could be a consequence of cell stress, cell cycle arrest, or indirect effects of CTCF loss on cellular physiology, rather than a direct result of chromatin reorganization. The authors acknowledge this limitation in the Discussion but do not adequately address it. The flow cytometry and spike-in RNA-seq experiments show a reduction in RNA, but they do not distinguish between reduced transcription and increased RNA degradation. Furthermore, the correlation between SALTA disassembly and gene expression changes (Fig. 4F) is modest (Pearson r not reported, only P = 0.017) and does not establish causality. Why it matters The claim that CTCF directly regulates global transcriptional capacity through chromatin organization is a central conclusion of the paper. If the observed reduction in RNA is due to indirect effects, the mechanistic link between CTCF, SALTAs, and transcription is weakened. Resolution test 1. Report the Pearson correlation coefficient for Fig. 4F. 2. Perform RNA stability assays (e.g., actinomycin D chase) to rule out increased degradation. 3. Use a more direct measure of transcription, such as nascent RNA sequencing (e.g., Bru-seq or PRO-seq), to confirm that the reduction is at the level of transcription. 4. Consider whether cell cycle analysis could explain the reduced RNA output (e.g., if CTCF depletion causes G1 arrest, cells would have less time to accumulate RNA). Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological validation / robustness Claim pointer "SALTAs represent genuine spatial aggregates of distantly located TLDs" (Results, Fig. 3) Evidence pointer Fig. 3G, Fig. S7B-E, Fig. S7F-G Concern The validation of SALTAs as genuine spatial structures relies heavily on comparisons with shuffled/shifted controls and comparisons with bulk multiway interaction datasets (GAM, SPRITE). However, the shuffled controls may not adequately account for the inherent biases in single-cell Hi-C data, such as the distance-dependent contact probability and the sparsity of contacts. The comparison with GAM/SPRITE is based on a small subset of domain triplets (11,097) and shows only modest overlap (fraction of alleles where all three domains are in the same SALTA). The authors do not report the absolute overlap fraction, making it difficult to assess the biological significance. Additionally, the downsampling analysis (Fig. S7H-L) shows that SALTA features are stable across a range of contact numbers, but the ARI and WS scores are not reported for the lowest contact numbers (e.g., 10,000), where sparsity is most severe. Why it matters If SALTAs are not robustly identified or are artifacts of the computational method, the subsequent analysis of their changes upon CTCF depletion is undermined. Resolution test 1. Report the absolute overlap fraction between SALTA-containing alleles and GAM/SPRITE triplets, not just the relative enrichment. 2. Provide ARI and WS scores for all downsampling levels, including the lowest (10,000 contacts). 3. Perform additional validation using independent single-cell Hi-C datasets or imaging-based approaches (e.g., DNA FISH) to confirm the spatial clustering of TLDs within SALTAs. 4. Test the sensitivity of SALTAFinder to the modularity threshold and the requirement for at least three TLDs. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretation / overclaim Claim pointer "CTCF stabilizes long-range active chromatin clusters" (Title, Abstract, Discussion) Evidence pointer Fig. 4A-G, Fig. S8, Fig. S9 Concern The manuscript concludes that CTCF "stabilizes" active SALTAs, but the evidence only shows that active SALTAs are less prevalent and more expanded upon CTCF loss. The term "stabilization" implies a direct structural role, but the observed changes could be secondary to reduced transcription or other indirect effects. The authors acknowledge this in the Discussion but the title and abstract present a more definitive claim. Furthermore, the classification of SALTAs into active, mixed, and inactive categories (C1-C7) is based on ChromHMM states from bulk data, which may not accurately reflect the chromatin state in individual cells. The K-means clustering of SALTAs is also sensitive to the number of clusters chosen, and the optimal number is not clearly justified. Why it matters Overstating the causal role of CTCF in stabilizing SALTAs could mislead the field. A more nuanced interpretation is warranted. Resolution test 1. Rephrase the title and abstract to reflect that CTCF loss is "associated with" destabilization of active SALTAs, rather than claiming direct stabilization. 2. Provide a more rigorous justification for the number of SALTA clusters (e.g., using the elbow method or silhouette analysis). 3. Consider using single-cell chromatin state data (if available) or at least discuss the limitations of using bulk ChromHMM states for single-cell analysis. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Statistical rigor / multiple testing Claim pointer "1947 bins showed significantly reduced PTLD-B and 1833 showed increases" (Results) Evidence pointer Fig. S4J, table S3 Concern The identification of bins with significantly changed TLD boundary probability (PTLD-B) is a key result, but the statistical method is not clearly described. The authors state that they used a "Wilcoxon test with FDR < 0.05" for compartment scores (Methods), but it is unclear if the same test was used for PTLD-B. Given the large number of bins tested (genome-wide at 50-kb resolution), multiple testing correction is critical. The authors do not report the number of tests or the FDR threshold used. Why it matters Without proper statistical rigor, the list of significantly changed bins may contain false positives, undermining the conclusion that boundaries are redistributed rather than lost. Resolution test 1. Clearly describe the statistical test used for PTLD-B analysis, including the number of tests and the FDR threshold. 2. Provide a volcano plot or similar visualization showing the distribution of P-values and effect sizes. 3. Consider using a more stringent threshold (e.g., FDR < 0.01) to ensure robustness.
